title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

title: Imaginary Expedition
location: Burdock Music Hall,1184 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON M6H 1N2, Canada
description:
Imaginary Expedition is a Toronto-based duo of Victoria Dobbs and Glyph Greenleaf who combine folk songwriting with early music composition techniques and intimate, unamplified performance practice. The ensemble draws people closer, quietly pushing the limits of what can be achieved with only their alto and baritone voices and a classical guitar. Their songs alternate between the lead vocalists, and gravitate toward duets with equal importance on both vocal lines.


The name Imaginary Expedition reflects the experience the duo creates. Their songs spark daydreams and send listeners on journeys through memory, grief, gratitude, and self-reflection. Their lyrics journey through emotional terrain shaped by the vivid changing seasons of the North, with imagery drawn from great lakes, old-growth forests, open prairies, wetlands, shield rock, and luminous skies.


Victoria and Glyph began writing together in August 2024 and performing together regularly in September 2025, after years of separate professional music careers. The duo has developed their live show and generated momentum through intimate listening rooms, festival stages, house concerts, and industry showcases. The duo has appeared at JP Music Festival in Boston (2025), and Toronto’s Winterfolk Blues + Roots Festival and Toronto Folk Festival (2026).


Their debut singles “Winter Lullaby” and “The Ones Who Are Gone” capture the acoustic realism of sitting in a room with the performers, whose voices move in harmony and counterpoint with Glyph’s lap-style classical guitar. The songs, which explore how we carry the memories of those we have lost, have received airplay on folk and indie radio in Canada, the USA, and Australia. With the support of a FACTOR Artist Development grant the duo has begun production of a full-length album in the same live-off-the-floor format.

*All films have closed captioning.

Movie info:

It might be November, but it’s still spooky season for us!

Messiah of Evil (1973) is a surreal, slow-burn horror film about a young woman who travels to the eerie seaside town of Point Dume, California, searching for her missing artist father. She finds his abandoned home and a disturbing diary warning of strange changes overtaking the town. As she investigates, she encounters increasingly bizarre residents, ritualistic behavior, and a growing sense that something ancient and horrifying is approaching. The film blends occult horror, zombies, and dreamlike imagery into an unsettling story of isolation and creeping doom.

This is the perfect movie to help us creep into the darker months.

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

title: Refrigerator Stories: A Search for Home
location: Tranzac,292 Brunswick Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 2M7, Canada
description:
(Living Room)

A new solo show by Jos Dirkx, directed by Reena Dutt, with music direction by Sacha Hoedemaker. Nine real-life stories, six original songs: starting in a classroom in Dakar with eleven kids from eleven countries, moving through Toronto, Helsinki, Juba and Athens, and arriving at a Dutch kitchen table where, at 39, Jos decides to step back on stage after all. A show about growing up between cultures, a voice that disappears and comes back, and love turning up when you least expect it. And what’s a refrigerator story? You’ll find out in the theatre.

The 2026 workshop performances will be the first time the complete show is performed for live audiences. In select venues, each performance is followed by a short conversation with the makers. The premiere will take place in 2027.

description:
The Toronto Workshop on Moral Psychology and Moral Theory is a forum for work at the intersection of empirical moral psychology and fundamental moral theory. The Workshop will take place on Saturday and Sunday, November 7 and 8, at the Jackman Humanities Building at the University of Toronto. All sessions will be entirely in person and will consist of 45-minute talks followed by 40-minute Q&A sessions. Any questions? It is free to attend the sessions. We ask only that you register by October 15 indicating your intention to attend.

title: UNHack
location: Room 313, Bergeron Centre, YorkU Keele Campus
description:
UNHack 2026 is a two-day hackathon hosted by YSpace and the Lassonde School of Engineering at York University, bringing together engineering students to tackle real-world challenges inspired by the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Participation does not need a startup idea, previous hackathon experience, or advanced technical skills. Through the programming you’ll be guided through a structured process that takes you from problem → idea → prototype → pitch, with support from mentors, facilitators, and technical experts along the way.
KEY DETAILS
📅 When

Saturday, November 7 – Sunday, November 8, 2026

📍 Where

Bergeron Centre for Engineering Excellence, York University

👥 Who Can Participate
UNHack is open to ANY undergraduate student at York University. You can register:

Individually – we’ll help match you with a team
With a pre-formed team of 3–5 students

💡 What You’ll Do
Over two days, you’ll:
1. Identify a problem
Explore selected UN Sustainable Development Goal challenge tracks and define a focused How Might We (HMW) problem statement.
2. Develop your solution
Generate ideas, understand your users, evaluate existing alternatives, and select a concept to pursue.
3. Build a prototype
Turn your idea into an achievable prototype or MVP with dedicated build time, workshops, technical support, and mentor office hours.
4. Pitch your solution
Develop and practice your pitch before presenting your solution to judges. Top teams will advance to the final round and pitch on the main stage.
🏆 PRIZES & OPPORTUNITIES

Cash prizes for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place teams
Mentorship from industry professionals and technical experts
Hands-on experience with design thinking, prototyping, and pitching
Experience Ventures: The first 60 eligible domestic students may receive. $325 upon successful completion of the hackathon and associated program requirements. Funding is first-come, first-served and subject to eligibility.

title: Question Everything: Evaluating in an era of bias, spin and social polarization
description:
Part of the Think, Research, Create: Intro to Library Research Series (3 out of 4)
Not all information is created equally—and not all search tools work the same way. This interactive workshop will help you compare popular tools for information discovery from AI to academic search platforms. You’ll learn the differences between misinformation, disinformation, malinformation, AI hallucinations and deepfakes. We’ll show you practical fact-checking tools and strategies to help you figure out what’s real and what’s not. You’ll also practice evaluating sources, including academic ones, so you can choose the most reliable information for your assignments. By the end, you’ll feel more confident navigating the information jungle!

title: Indigenous Beading Workshop: Poppy
description:
Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026
Time: 11:00 am – 2:00 pm
Location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St. W.
Tickets: $65 
In honour of Remembrance Day and National Indigenous Veterans Day, join Natalie Ortiz for a meaningful afternoon of beading, reflection, and remembrance. In this hands-on workshop, participants will create a beautiful beaded poppy while learning about the significance of poppies as symbols of remembrance and the important contributions and sacrifices of Indigenous veterans. 
Guided step-by-step by Natalie, guests will explore traditional beading techniques in a welcoming and supportive environment. This workshop offers an opportunity to connect through artmaking while honouring histories, stories, and acts of service that continue to shape communities across Canada. 
Recommended for participants 16+. Includes instruction, materials, and access to all current exhibitions.  
BUY YOUR TICKETS  

ABOUT NATALIE ORTIZ: 
 
Natalie Ortiz is a Toronto-based Indigenous artist. Her work focuses on handmade jewelry, moccasins, and leatherwork. Natalie is Anishinaabe of Wauzhushk Onigum Nation and of Peruvian decent. Her art carries deep meaning connected to her roots, reflecting the traditions and teachings passed down through generations. She learned beading and moccasin-making through traditional teachings. She has been making moccasins for five years, and every pair is crafted with intention, meant to be worn and appreciated by anyone who connects with them. Follow Natalie on social media for moccasins and leatherwork at @natymocs. Her jewelry can be found on Oliva’s Jewelry and @olivasjewelry.

title: NEW TRAIL! 🍂 From Scarborough to North York: The Fall Colours Trail Walk 🌈
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍂 From Scarborough to North York: The Fall Colours Trail Walk 🌈

### A Scenic Fall Adventure Through Trails, Ravines & Toronto History

Toronto has some wonderful natural spaces tucked between its neighbourhoods, and this walk connects two of them into one longer adventure!

We’ll begin in Scarborough, exploring the **Gatineau Corridor Trail**, with its wildflowers, tall grasses, and green spaces where nature is allowed to grow a little more freely. 🍁 From there, we’ll make our way along some city streets before connecting with another trail system and continuing through the surrounding ravines toward the **Rainbow Tunnel**.

The tunnel is an unusual piece of Toronto history, painted in 1971 by teenager B.C. Johnson as a tribute to his friend Sigred, who died in a car accident. Although the artwork has seen better days, we’ll make a quick stop to see it before continuing toward our final destination.

We’ll finish at **Shops at Don Mills**, where anyone who wants to can join us for coffee, a pastry, or something to eat after the walk. ☕🥐
This is a longer outing than some of our regular walks, but we’ll take our time, enjoy the scenery, and have a break along the way.

***

### 🚶‍♂️ What We’ll Do

Along the route, we’ll:

* Explore the Gatineau Corridor Trail and its naturalized green spaces 🌼
* Walk through parks and neighbourhood streets
* Take a break midway through the walk
* Connect with the Moccasin Trail and surrounding ravine paths 🌳
* Stop briefly at the Rainbow Tunnel 🌈
* Continue to Shops at Don Mills
* Finish with an optional coffee or snack with the group ☕

The walk should take approximately **3 hours**, depending on the pace of the group and the conditions along the route.
**Please note:** This is a point-to-point walk. We will not return to our starting location at Dollar Tree. At the end, I’ll help anyone who needs assistance figuring out their transit options.

***

### ☀️ Weather & Expectations

This walk takes place in typical Toronto weather conditions. Please dress appropriately for the forecast and wear comfortable walking shoes.
The route includes a mix of paved streets, trails, and potentially uneven or unpaved surfaces. There will be some distance to cover, so this walk is best suited to people who are comfortable walking for around three hours, with breaks.

This is a social walk, not a race. We’ll keep a steady pace and make time to enjoy the surroundings.

🌦️ **This event happens rain or shine!**

***

### 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Starting Location:** Outside the Dollar Tree near Kennedy Station
🫎 **Look for me wearing my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** 11:00 AM
I will only wait 5 minutes.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** Shops at Don Mills, North York
🚇 **Transit:** We’ll finish near the Eglinton line. I’ll help anyone who needs directions for getting home by transit.

***

### 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer to [mathewmaclean@hotmail.com](mailto:mathewmaclean@hotmail.com)**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing walks and other events throughout Toronto.

***

### ☕ After the Walk

Once we reach Shops at Don Mills, anyone who wants to continue the outing can join us for coffee, pastries, or a bite to eat.
It's a chance to relax, chat, and get to know one another after our walk. Participation is optional.

***

### 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥨 A snack
🧥 Weather-appropriate clothing
📱 Your phone or camera for photos

***

### 🌈 Who Is This For?

This walk is great for:

* People who enjoy discovering hidden parts of Toronto
* Anyone interested in local history and unusual landmarks
* Walkers who enjoy exploring trails and ravines
* People looking to meet others and make friends
* Anyone who wants to spend a few hours outdoors enjoying the fall colours

The trails and Rainbow Tunnel are part of the adventure, but **the people you meet along the way are the real experience.**

***

**REMEMBER:** You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**
Questions? Post on the event wall or email **[torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com](mailto:torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com)**

**Come for the trails.**
**Stay for the conversation.**
**Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.** 🍂💛

description: This listing is for a three session Beginner Spinning Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Saturday November 7th, 14, 21st from 12:30pm - 2:00pm Learn how to transform fibre into yarn with our drop spindle class! In this class you will learn how to use a drop spindle to spin starting with woolly fibre and ending with a completed, ready to use yarn. You will learn how to spin a single ply yarn, how to spin a 2-ply yarn using the Andean Plying method, and how to chain ply for a 3-ply yarn over three classes. We will discuss spinning basics as well as different types of yarn, fibres, processing tools, and preparations and how these affect the finished yarn. Knitting, crochet, spinning, dyeing, embroidery, hand sewing, machine sewing - Anna has a voracious appetite for learning new textile techniques. With a background in textile artifact conservation, Anna explores the craft, history, and science behind fibre arts. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . title: 2SLGBTQ+ aging with and into difference(s) | Film Screening with CRIP Lab and Tangled Art + Disability
description:
Presented by CRIP Lab, University of Guelph & Tangled Arts + Disabilty

The Special Edition of CRIP Lab with film screenings is here! We have been talking about this since our last two gatherings. Jami Mcfarland and Patricia Ginn would also be joining us. Very excited to see the movies with you all! This event is online only . More details about the event are below, along with the zoom links. Please feel free to extend the invitation to your friends 🙂 We would love to have them join us for this beautiful event. Saturday, Nov 7, 1-2:30 p.m. Presented by CRIP Lab, University of Guelph & Tangled Arts + Disabilty Film Screenings from a study led by Jami Mcfarland : 2SLGBTQ+ aging with and into difference(s) Storytellers' names and titles: Patricia Derouin’s “Not Dead Yet” (8 mins) Michael Dion’s “Why Didn’t Anyone Tell Me About Aging” (6 mins, 39 secs) Rev. Marcie Wexler’s “Solitaire Road” (6 mins, 20 secs) Bernie Thompson’s “New Beginnings” (9 mins, 42 secs) Rita OLink’s “I’m Not Going to Run, I’m Not Going to Hide” (8 mins, 9 secs) Don Turner’s “A Long Journey Into Aging” (7 mins, 23 secs) David Drinkwalter’s “My Life in the Lost and Found Department” (6 mins, 36 secs) Dar Hansen’s “Dar’s Story” (6 mins, 48 secs) Jo Brook’s “A Fae-ry Tale” (8 mins, 55 secs) These stories came from a SSHRC-funded study, "(Eng)Aging Crip Rainbow Representations: 2SLGBTQ+ Disabled Older Adults Access the Arts and Create Belonging through Digital Storytelling," which sought to create diverse representations at the nexus of 2SLGBTQ+ aging, disability, and illness. Some storytellers chose to explore disability and illness directly in their stories, while others focused on other parts of their identities in their stories. Jami Mcfarland is the PI of this study, but there are several other academics contributing to it: Carla Rice, Nadine Changfoot, Celeste Pang, and Nicole Dalmer), and an excellent RA (Andrea Keber. Funded by SSHRC, the study was created in collaboration with Re-Vision: The Centre for Art and Social Justice at the University of Guelph. location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Doubles: A Panel Talk About the Film, Diversity & Indo-Caribbean Voices
description:
Join us for an extraordinary evening with the actors and production team behind the six-time, award-nominated film
Doubles
, where diversity meets imagination, identity meets history and rarely heard Indo-Caribbean voices come together to celebrate the power of storytelling.
The Canadian drama film, Doubles, set in both Trinidad and Toronto, explores the relationship between a son and his estranged father. When tragedy strikes, Dhani, a Doubles stand operator dreaming of owning his own restaurant, must leave Trinidad to find his father, whom he hasn't seen in years. Their reunion brings deeply held feelings to the surface as unexpected revelations change their lives forever.
Presented by the
Canadian Caribbean Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
, this panel will feature:
Mark Sirju
, Producer
Errol Sitahal
, Actor portraying Ragbir
Premika Leo
, Actor portraying Skye
Kenneth Mohabir
, comedian, actor, and producer, will moderate the discussion.
The film is approximately 1 hour 29 minutes long, followed by a discussion with the panelists about the importance of Indo-Caribbean representation, behind-the-scenes stories about the film, and an audience Q&A.
Free program. Please register. Doors open at 1:45 pm. At 2:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached, with light refreshments (while supplies last).
Organization Info:
The
Canadian Caribbean Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
is a community organization representing Indians (currently referred to as South Asians) of various ethnicities, regions, and faiths, who are the descendants of the indentured labourers taken by the British to their colonies in the Caribbean and around the world. Their mission is to share their stories of struggle, resilience and contributions across the Caribbean and here in Canada.

title: Introduction to Chainmail Workshop
location: Lillian H. Smith, Bagshaw Room, 1st floor.
description:
Chainmail, the ancient art of linking metal rings together in a chain or mesh weave, has a long history within cultural practices from all over the world. These days you might not need a piece of armour to protect yourself during a swordfight, but you still might want to know how to make some - whether for yourself or to deck out a favourite toy! Or, maybe you want to make some unique jewelry: bracelets, necklaces, or earrings. Why not both?
Registration for both sessions is required:
1st session, Nov 7: Basics! Opening and closing rings, Japanese 1-in-1, 2-in-2, or 3-in-3 chain weave, attaching clasps. Make a bracelet or a short necklace.
2nd session, Nov 21: Pick 1 option - barrel or box chain weave, or 4-1 European mesh weave. Make a bracelet, a short necklace, or a base for a larger piece.
Please note that chainmail requires repetitive hand motions, gripping, and close visual attention to detail.
These sessions are oriented towards beginners but more advanced learners are also welcome.

title: The U of T, Yorkville and Rochdale College (MEGA-TOUR)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**This is a revised route for 2026 to take in the history of the historic Rochdale College!**

On March 15, 1827, a royal charter was issued by King George IV, for the establishment of King's College. The charter was the result of the efforts of John Strachan, the Anglican Bishop of Toronto, the College's first president.

King's College was a religious institution tied to the Church of England and the Family Compact. In 1849, the newly elected government of Canada voted to rename the College, University of Toronto and broke with the church. Strachan resigned to open Trinity College as a private seminary.

University College was created as a branch of University of Toronto. During the American Civil War, the threat of Union blockade prompted the creation of the University Rifle Corps, which saw action against the Fenians on the Niagara border in 1866.

Founded in 1830 by Joseph Bloor, and William Botsford Jarvis, the Village of Yorkville was muddy York's northern residential suburb.

With historic establishments like The Red Lion Inn, Yorkville Town Hall or even the fierce political radical William Lyon Mackenzie, it was here that notoriety was achieved, in Yorkville itself.

Omnibus horse drawn streetcar service started in 1849 to connect the old St. Lawrence Market in Toronto with Yorkville, and by 1853, the population of the village had reached 1,000 residents.

By the 1870s, Potter's Field, a cemetery stretching west of Yonge Street at Bloor Street was closed, and the remains moved to other area cemeteries. Yorkville was growing fast, and soon Toronto was ready to pull the neighbourhood into its orbit. On February 1, 1883, Yorkville's name changed officially. It was now known as St. Paul's Ward!

This walking tour is for all fitness levels and skills. Please dress for the weather. The extensive walking tour begins at the Queen's Park SUBWAY Station at the **southwest corner** of University Avenue and College Street adjacent to the Tim Horton's at the corner.

The walk ends at the site of Historic Rochdale College at Bloor and Huron!

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person!

title: TORONTO BOOK LAUNCH - TWO DAYS IN MAYARO, BY PAMELA MORDECAI
description:
📚🚀🌴A Different Booklist & Goose Lane Editions are proud to present celebrated author Pamela Mordecai in conversation with journalist Neil Armstrong for the launch of her new collection of Caribbean diasporic short fiction, TWO DAYS IN MAYARO!
Jamaican Canadian Pamela Mordecai's first short story collection, PINK ICING received glowing reviews, and her debut novel, RED JACKET, was shortlisted for the Rogers Writers’ Trust Fiction Prize. She has published nine collections of poetry and books for children. Weaving old time and contemporary stories, TWO DAYS IN MAYARO, Pamela's second collection of short fiction, depicts the struggles, triumphs, and humour of diaspora life, creating a world powered by unforgettable characters in language that sings.
Look forward to a live reading by Pamela and a Q&A. Special guest writer Nalo Hopkinson will introduce the author, and Neil Armstrong will conduct the interview. See you there - #ReadDifferently!📚

description: This listing is for a one session Cable Class. The class will be held in person at Bistitchual on Saturday November 7 from 2:30pm-4:30pm Have you been fantasizing about the cable sweater of your dreams? Take a step towards making that dream a reality with our Cables Class and learn the secrets of the deceptively simple yet hugely impactful cable knitting technique. In this class you will learn cable basics which will allow you to tackle any cable project. Students will work through a small pattern that exemplifies cable techniques. If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. There will be a four person maximum for each class. Please pre-book your spot to let us know you are coming! About the Instructor: If idle hands are the Devil’s tools, he hasn’t much to do with Anna (she/they.) Anna’s grandmother taught her to knit as a toddler and she hasn’t put the yarn down since. Knitting, crochet, spinning, dyeing, embroidery, hand sewing, machine sewing - Anna has a voracious appetite for learning new textile techniques. With a background in textile artifact conservation, Anna explores the craft, history, and science behind fibre arts. description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:

title: Fast Friends: Meet New People, Make Connections & Play 50+ Board Games | 25–45
description:
Toronto 20's to 50's Singles Social (4000+)
Making new friends as an adult can be harder than it seems. You want to meet new people, have good conversations and build genuine connections — but knowing where to start isn't always easy.

🤝 That's where Fast Friends comes in.

Join us at Stout Irish Pub for a professionally hosted social evening designed to make meeting people feel natural and enjoyable. With guided conversations, rotations and fun themed connection rounds, you'll have an easy way to meet a variety of people, discover shared interests and start building new friendships — even if you arrive on your own.

And the evening doesn't end with the hosted rounds! Stay for 50+ board games, drinks, food and Stout's After Dark Specials. 🎲🍻

🎟️ Book Early & Save: [https://toronto7thnov.eventbrite.co.uk](https://toronto7thnov.eventbrite.co.uk)
You can pay securely online with any debit or credit card through PayPal — no PayPal account required.

Advance tickets are cheaper and help us plan the right space and group size for a comfortable evening.

Early Bird: CAD $10 \| Regular: CAD $15 \| At the Door: CAD $20 cash

🤝 The Evening
7:00 PM — Welcome & Settle In
Meet your host, Kruttika, grab a drink and get comfortable.
Whether you've recently moved to Toronto or have lived here for years, it's a chance to step out, meet some new faces and enjoy a different kind of Saturday evening.
Coming alone? You're very welcome — many guests attend solo, and our host will help you settle in and get connected.

7:30–8:30 PM — Hosted Fast Friends
Meeting people doesn't have to mean approaching a room full of strangers and hoping a conversation takes off.
Our host guides you through short conversations and rotations, so you can meet a variety of people throughout the evening. You don't have to worry about who to approach or what to say next — the structure makes it easier to get involved and discover who you connect with.
✨ Themed Connection Rounds
We'll add interactive prompts and themed conversation challenges to help you discover shared interests, swap stories and find unexpected common ground.
From travel and food to music, hobbies and weekend adventures, these rounds help move conversations beyond the usual small talk.

🎲 8:30 PM onwards — 50+ Board Games & Socialising
Why end the evening just as you're getting to know people?
Stout has more than 50 board games available, giving you an easy way to keep socialising after the hosted rounds. Join a game, meet others around the table, share a few laughs, grab another drink or simply continue a conversation.
You don't need to be a board-game expert. It's all about having fun together and giving new connections more time to grow.

🍻 Stay for Stout's After Dark Specials
If you're planning to stay later, Stout's After Dark Special runs from 9–11 PM, with $7 beers and $7 highballs, among other specials.
It's a great way to extend your evening, relax with the people you've met and enjoy more of Stout's lively pub atmosphere.

❤️ Why Come Along?
✔️ Meet 20+ new people in one evening
✔️ Professionally hosted conversations and rotations
✔️ Interactive themed rounds to spark better conversations
✔️ 50+ board games at Stout 🎲
✔️ Stout's After Dark Specials from 9–11 PM 🍻
✔️ Reserved space for our group
✔️ Relaxed Irish pub atmosphere
✔️ An opportunity to meet members from across our Toronto Meetup communities
✔️ Solo attendees welcome
✔️ Designed for ladies and gents aged 25–45
✔️ Friendship-focused — not a dating event

📍 Why Stout Irish Pub?
Located at 221 Carlton Street, Stout offers a relaxed, welcoming pub atmosphere with food, drinks and an impressive selection of more than 50 board games.
It's a great setting for an evening that starts with hosted conversations and continues with board games, laughter and more time to get to know the people you've met.

👥 Who Is It For?
You don't need to be new to Toronto, belong to an existing group or know anyone attending.
Whether you're looking to build a social circle, meet people beyond work, make friends after moving to the city or simply enjoy a different kind of Saturday night, you're welcome.
Come by yourself or bring a friend. We'll help make the introductions easier.

🌍 About Fast Friends
For over 10 years, Fast Friends has been bringing people together through professionally hosted social events in 30+ cities worldwide.
Our goal is simple: make meeting new people easier, more relaxed and more enjoyable.

Come for the conversations. Stay for the board games. Leave with new connections. ❤️
Come solo. We'll guide the experience. You make the connections. 🤝

title: SPECIMEN: Science Fiction on Stage
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

We've been invited to see an original sci-fi play called SPECIMEN at Axis Theatre Company in Greenwich Village with discounted tickets for just $10!
.
Written and directed by Randall Sharp, SPECIMEN takes place aboard a damaged research spacecraft, where a crew struggles to make sense of their new reality. TheaterScene calls it a "... darkly absurd sci-fi fever dream…" that "...arrives like a transmission from a dying satellite: garbled, abrasive, funny, ugly, unexpectedly moving, and very much alive…"
.
The production is a dark comedy and has an avant-garde, 1970s sci-fi feel. From [their website](https://axiscompany.org/mainstage.php), SPECIMEN "...draws from the tradition of downtown experimental and absurdist theatre, blending visual storytelling, heightened performance, dark humor, and immersive design..."
.
Tickets are usually $40, so this is a big discount to see a new, well-reviewed show.
.

.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

Directed by Bonnie Duff

title: Fall Hiking Glen Major Forest/Brock Tract 13 km 9 AM START
description: Glen Major Forest/Brock Tract Loop The Glen Major Forest is more than 3700 acres of land located on the Oak Ridges Moraine in the headwaters of the Duffins Creek Watershed. This area consists of mixed coniferous/ deciduous forests and a gravel pit once operated in the Glen Major site and is currently being restored. The remainder of the property complex was previously used for agriculture and contains a variety of habitat including forest, meadows and wetlands. Old farm roads and farm building foundations are still visible. This hike has lots of elevation changes and I think that most hikers will find the forest quite beautiful but strenuous. It is a hike worth doing. Distance: 13 km Route:...

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🍂 Crothers Woods Fall Hike & Ice Cream Treat! 🍦
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
## 🍂 **Crothers Woods Fall Hike & Ice Cream Treat!** 🍦

Toronto doesn’t have many true hiking trails — but Crothers Woods is one of the best! This beautiful wooded trail is especially stunning in the fall, with the leaves turning every shade of red and gold.
We’ll start by walking along **Broadview Avenue to Pottery Road**, heading down the hill to meet the **Don Valley Trail**. From there, we’ll join the **Crothers Woods Trail**, take in the fall colours, stop for a short break, and then walk back.

There are a few light hills — and one big one at the very end (Pottery Road, I’m looking at you!) — but don’t worry, there’s a sweet reward waiting. After all that hard work, we’ll stop for **Dairy Queen ice cream**!
This hike is a bit more challenging than some of our regular walks, but totally worth it for the views (and the ice cream).

**This event happens rain or shine!**

***

### 📍 **Meetup Details**

**Meeting Spot:** Right outside **Broadview Subway Station** — I’ll be the one wearing the **Moose Hat!** 🦌
**Ending Spot:** Broadview Subway Station
**Meetup Fee:** $5 (cash in person or e-transfer to **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**)

***

### 🕒 **Timing**

11:00am and I will only wait 5mins — the hike should take about **2 hours**.
You can leave anytime you like if you need to head back early.

***

### 🥾 **What to Bring**

* Water
* Good walking or hiking shoes
* A snack
* A positive attitude (and maybe room for ice cream!)

***

### ⚠️ **A Quick Note**

Sometimes things come up and I might need to cancel or reschedule. Please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

***

### 👋 **About This Group**

This group is open to **everyone** — whether you’re single or not, new to the city, or just looking to be social and make friends.
We also host **movies, walks, hikes, arts & culture events, and restaurant outings**!
You can RSVP ahead of time **or just show up** if you’re not sure you can make it — we’re flexible like that.

***

**Organizer:** Mathew

title: Landmarks 6: Gladstone Hotel to The Edgewater Hotel Via Gutta Percha
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Toronto is a city that hides its history in plain sight. Beneath the glass towers are layers of stories — grand hotels that vanished overnight, political scandals whispered through stone corridors, theatres that once glittered under gaslight, and laneways where the city first learned how to become a metropolis.

This new Toronto History Walks tour invites the walker to slow down, and see the city differently.

Let's return to a bygone era: late 1930s. Parkdale would already have had a long fascinating history behind it, but you would also be looking at a neighbourhood that was changing with the times. One of the most interesting examples was the Edgewater Hotel, built in 1939 at 14 Roncesvalles Avenue, at The Queensway.

It was built by Fred Hammer and became part of a very busy transportation hub, sitting beside the Sunnyside Bus Terminal. The building has survived, although the Edgewater name eventually disappeared and the hotel went through several incarnations. It is a wonderful reminder that Parkdale's history isn't just Victorian, there is twentieth-century history here as well.

And then we come to the Gladstone Hotel, which is one of those buildings that almost seem to have been watching the neighbourhood change. The hotel we see today dates from 1889 and was designed by Toronto architect George Martell Miller in the Richardsonian Romanesque style. Its location was absolutely perfect for business: it stood across from the Parkdale railway station, and was close to the Exhibition grounds. Travelling salesmen, railway workers, visitors to the CNE and commercial travellers could all find shelter here.

The original owner was Susanna Robinson, who was left a widow with thirteen children before construction of the hotel was completed.
The Gladstone tells us something important about Parkdale itself. For decades it was a working-class gathering place, and as the factories and industries changed, so did the fortunes of the hotel. The great tower once had a cupola that could be seen from a distance, but that disappeared in the 1940s. By the later twentieth century the hotel had fallen on hard times and had developed a much different reputation. Yet it never completely lost its role as a community gathering place.

Eventually it was restored and reinvented, becoming part of the artistic and cultural life of Queen Street West.

And finally, we get to one of the great industrial stories of old Parkdale — the Gutta Percha & Rubber Manufacturing Company. Established here in 1883 on West Lodge Avenue, the factory became one of the largest employers in the neighbourhood and, at its height, the largest rubber manufacturer in Canada. They made all sorts of rubber products — hose, belting, boots, footwear, mats and eventually products connected with the rapidly growing automobile industry.

The factory operated until 1960, when changing technology, synthetic rubber and competition finally brought its long Parkdale story to an end. Three places — the Edgewater, the Gladstone and Gutta Percha — give us three very different Parkdales: the Parkdale of travel and transportation, the Parkdale of hotels and community life, and the Parkdale of factories and working people. Put them together and you begin to see just how fascinating this neighbourhood really is.

This walking tour begins at The Gladstone Hotel at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Gladstone Avenue, one block east of Dufferin Street. We end at the corner of Queen Street West and Roncesvalles Avenue.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/



Exhibition Hours

Wednesdays & Thursdays 1 to 6 pm

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

The roof is banging.

French downstairs.

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

title: Nov 9 - Agentic Labeling for Specialized Visual Data
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 09, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/when-prompting-beats-training-agentic-labeling-for-specialized-visual-data-november-9-2026)**

Frontier multimodal models handle familiar concepts well and struggle on niche ones: sorting drill-core samples into 35 geological classes, or telling adhesion from scarring on a ceramic substrate. Our study across 11 specialized visual datasets in manufacturing inspection, geology, and medical imaging found that a few labeled examples in the prompt can close much of that gap, and it also found where that stops working.

**What you’ll learn:**

* Niche versus hard: how in-context examples supply domain knowledge a model is missing, and how to tell a niche task from a genuinely hard one
* What the study measured: on an industrial defect task, one labeled example per class raised macro-F1 from 34% to 59% with no fine-tuning, while on other tasks trained specialists pulled ahead at 5 to 10 examples per class
* Building a few-shot labeling task: define classes, pick reference examples, preview predictions on a small batch, and refine the instructions
* Finding the crossover point: when to stop prompting a foundation model and train a specialist on bootstrapped labels
* Running it on your own data: attendees get free GPU compute from Nebius to try the workflow after the session

title: Recovery College Co Design Course For Graduate & Mature Students)
description:
Are you a graduate or mature student interested in shaping mental health and well‑being programming that reflects your lived experience at York University? This co‑design opportunity is for you.
In collaboration with Ontario Shores Centre for Mental Health Sciences, Student Counselling, Health & Well‑being (SCHW) is expanding our recovery college programming— a series of health and well‑being workshops designed to help students thrive amid the unique pressures of advanced study, research, caregiving, work and life transitions.
What will we do?
You and a small group of fellow graduate and mature students will work alongside SCHW and Ontario Shores to co‑create the next set of recovery college workshops launching in Winter/Spring 2027. Together, you will shape workshop topics, content and learning activities and how sessions are delivered and facilitated.
What will we learn?

Recovery college principles and how education rooted in lived experience supports mental health
Co‑design methods for building impactful student‑centered programming
How to draw on your own experiences navigating academic and life‑stage pressures as a source of expertise
How to collaborate as part of a design team to create accessible, empowering mental health workshops

Program Details
This 5‑week co‑design series runs virtually on Mondays from 1:15 to 2:15 PM, from November 9 to December 7. Participation is open to all graduate and mature students.
Honorarium
In appreciation for your support, participants will receive $25 loaded directly to their YU card for each session attended in full (up to $125 for completing all five sessions).
Note: Co‑Design sessions run for one hour. To receive the honorarium for a session, you must attend the full session. If you are unable to attend the full hour or experience technical difficulties, please contact Holly Stacey directly at hstacey@yorku.ca ( mailto:hstacey@yorku.ca ).

Space is limited (maximum 12 participants) and offered on a first‑come, first‑served basis. Registration is open to mature undergraduate students, graduate students and School of Continuing Studies students. If spots are full but you would like to be added to a waiting list in the event of cancellations, please contact Holly Stacey at hstacey@yorku.ca ( mailto:hstacey@yorku.ca ). title: Chang Goo Kim (Princeton University)
description:
Title: From Resolved ISM Physics to Galaxy Formation Models: Star Formation, Winds, and Cosmic Rays

Abstract: Galaxy formation simulations cannot resolve the interstellar medium (ISM), where stars form and feedback acts, so
star formation and feedback enter them through subgrid models that are traditionally based on the local gas density
and calibrated empirically. In this talk, I will show how we use high-fidelity simulations of the multiphase ISM to
bridge this gap. The TIGRESS frameworks model kiloparsec-scale patches of galactic disks with resolved supernova
remnants, and now include UV radiation transfer, non-equilibrium photochemistry, and cosmic-ray transport with
self-consistent scattering rates. From these simulations we identify robust physical principles and turn them into
subgrid models. First, in the pressure-regulated, feedback-modulated (PRFM) theory, the star formation rate follows
the weight of the ISM that feedback must support. The resulting star formation–pressure relation agrees with
observations of nearby galaxies, and implemented in galaxy formation simulations, it predicts star formation rates
that differ from density-based recipes. Second, galactic winds are multiphase: cool gas carries most of the mass and
hot gas most of the energy, and subgrid wind models built on this picture regulate galaxy growth preventively,
through the circumgalactic medium. Third, cosmic rays leave star formation rates and wind launching unchanged but
accelerate cool gas above the disk, producing more mass-loaded outflows. Finally, I will introduce LIT (Learning the
ISM with TIGRESS), a simulation suite across galactic environments designed to connect ISM simulations with
observations.

title: Changing the Narrative: Toronto’s Indigenous – Settler History
location: Toronto Reference Library, 1st Floor, Beeton Hall
description:
Learn more about Toronto's multifaceted Indigenous history, which has often been ignored or minimized due to the telling of the region's history only from settler perspectives. Join us for a panel discussion about a public history project that worked with five local First Nations to create a more accurate and inclusive story of the region's past, and is transforming the way settlement of 19th century Ontario is represented at The Village at Black Creek (formerly Black Creek Pioneer Village).
Changing the Narrative: Reconnecting Settler and Indigenous Histories at Black Creek Pioneer Village was a collaborative project of York University historians, The Village at Black Creek, Jumblies Theatre, and the Mississaugas of the Credit, Chippewas of Rama, Six Nations of the Grand River, Chippewas of Georgina Island, and Mississaugas of Scugog Island First Nations.
This panel discussion will share research highlights, reflect on the process of collaboration, and explore how the project is expanding and enriching storytelling at one of the region’s prime living history museums.
The project’s findings have also been published in Where Histories Meet: Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area, by Victoria Freeman. The book explores this history from multiple perspectives in an accessible and richly illustrated format and includes excerpts from interviews with twenty Indigenous elders and knowledge keepers. It was nominated for a
2026 City of Toronto Book Award
and is the winner of the
2026 Heritage Toronto Book Award.
Panel members include:
Victoria      Freeman
, historical researcher and author of
Where Histories Meet:      Indigenous and Settler Encounters in the Toronto Area
.
Jennifer      Bonnell
, professor in the Department of History at York University and the      lead of the Changing the Narrative Project.
Allison      White
, curator at The Village at Black Creek (Toronto and Region      Conservation Authority).
Darin      Wybenga
, heritage interpreter for the Mississaugas of the Credit First      Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the Changing the      Narrative project.
Lauri      Hoeg
, Anishinaabe artist and cultural advisor from the Chippewas of      Georgina Island First Nation, and member of the Research Committee for the      Changing the Narrative project.
The panel discussion will last approximately 60 minutes, followed by a Q&A with audience members. No registration required.

title: Hank Idsinga: The High Road
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space, North York Central Library (5120 Yonge St), Lower Level
description:
TPL presents retired homicide detective and author Hank Idsinga in conversation with Wendy Gillis at the North York Central Library's Concourse Event Space.
In his bestselling memoir
The High Road: Confessions of a Homicide Cop
, Idsinga takes readers behind the crime scene tape and into the mean streets of Toronto's most notorious murders. Teaming up with partners including future police chief Mark Saunders, Idsinga built a reputation for excellent recall and sharp instinct, finding motive and method faster than most. As the public face of that investigation, Idsinga remained strong and compassionate before the cameras, even as the police force faced fierce criticism over its handling of the case.
How do homicide detectives carry the weight of the cases they never solve? What does real accountability within policing actually look like, and why does it matter? And what can three decades on the front lines of Toronto's worst crimes teach us about justice, institutional trust, and the human cost of violence?
Join veteran crime reporter Wendy Gillis in conversation with Hank Idsinga for a gripping, candid evening inside the world of Canada's most storied homicide unit.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Hank Idsinga
Wendy Gillis

The High Road

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: The Certificate in Personal Wellness for Grad Students
description:
The Certificate in Personal Wellness is a supportive and enriching experience designed to nurture personal well-being and promote balance in everyday life. Participants will explore practical, evidence-informed strategies for reducing stress, understanding and managing negative thought patterns, and building emotional resilience. Drawing from the field of positive psychology, the series introduces empowering practices such as mindfulness, gratitude, and self-compassion—skills that encourage greater self-awareness, inner calm, and a more compassionate relationship with oneself. Aspects of Cognitive Behavioural Therapy and Dialetical Behaviour Therapy will be included.



Dates: October 20, 27, November 3, 10 & 17​

title: Your Health Matters: Diabetes Myths and Facts
description:
Living with diabetes or prediabetes can come with a lot of information about what to eat, what to avoid, and how to manage your blood sugar. With so much advice out there, it can be difficult to separate fact from fiction or know where to focus.
Join Catherine Cai, Registered Dietitian and Certified Diabetes Educator, for a practical and interactive session that separates fact from fiction and explores realistic ways to better understand and manage diabetes and prediabetes.
What to Expect
Understanding Blood Sugar:
Learn what your levels mean and how an A1C test provides a picture of your average levels over time.
Diabetes Myths and Facts:
Explore common myths      and misconceptions about diabetes and separate fact from fiction.
Lifestyle and Blood Sugar:
Learn how sleep,      stress and other lifestyle factors can affect blood sugar.
Building Balanced Meals:
Learn practical ways      to build balanced, diabetes-friendly meals.
Balance, Not Perfection:
Explore how balance      and consistency can support diabetes management without striving for      perfection.
About the Presenter
Catherine Cai is a Registered Dietitian and Certified Diabetes Educator at Crosstown Family Health Team. She provides practical information and guidance to help people better understand nutrition and support their health.
This program is presented by Toronto Public Library in collaboration with the West Toronto Ontario Health Team (OHT), a network of over 40 local health and social service providers working together to improve the health and well-being of communities in West Toronto.
Your Health Matters
This program is part of Toronto Public Library’s
Your Health Matters
initiative, which offers trusted health programs and resources to help people make informed decisions about their health. Learn more by exploring the
Your Health Matters web page
.

title: Building AI solutions for small businesses with Microsoft 365 Copilot
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Artificial intelligence is no longer just for large enterprises. Microsoft 365 Copilot gives small businesses access to AI-powered tools that can help improve productivity, automate routine tasks, and free up time to focus on growth. In this introductory session, attendees will learn how Microsoft 365 Copilot integrates with familiar Microsoft 365 applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams.

Through practical demonstrations and real-world business scenarios, participants will discover how Copilot can help create content, analyze data, summarize meetings, manage email, and streamline everyday workflows. The session also introduces best practices for responsible AI adoption, effective prompting, and identifying business processes where AI can deliver immediate value. Attendees will leave with a clear understanding of how to get started with Microsoft 365 Copilot and where to continue learning through Microsoft Learn and official Microsoft documentation.

Who should attend small business owners Entrepreneurs Startup founders Business managers Marketing and sales professionals Anyone looking to improve productivity using Microsoft 365 Copilot Learning objectives Understand what Microsoft 365 Copilot is and how it works.

title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion.
Python Essentials 1
is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions.
Python Essentials 2
is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: Skyward Steps:Mixed Media 3D Dance of Freedom
description:

The 3D ladder becomes both a stage and a storytelling element, expressing freedom, creativity, and harmony between humans and the natural world.

title: Writing Place Workshop with Marc Nair
location: Toronto Reference Library, Third-Floor, Discussion Room
description:
​This writing workshop revolves around writing place, where participants will write poems or flash fiction about a place that is near and dear to them. Participants take an observational narrative approach to writing about place, employing selected poetry and flash fiction techniques. They will take turns sharing their work while the facilitator, poet Marc Nair, offers on-the-spot feedback.
This event will feature a
90 minute Workshop:
Introduction - facilitator (Marc) will invite participants to name their favorite place and expand on why it is so significant for them.
Facilitator will begin by sharing a couple of poems that are rooted in a sense of place, exploring how the poems are written in order to offer concrete suggestions for participants.
Participants then engage in a free writing exercise to generate content about a particular place. Facilitator will then invite some participants to share and suggest how to shape the content using a 'seed' idea or image from the free writing.
Facilitator will also talk about flash fiction (100-200 word) stories as an alternative to the poem. Facilitator will share some examples.
Participants will write their own poem or flash fiction over the next twenty minutes.
They will take turns sharing their work while the facilitator offers on the spot feedback
Marc Nair is an artist, educator and cultural entrepreneur from Singapore who is currently based in Toronto, Canada.
Registration is required.

title: Author Talk featuring Dan Jones
description:
[at Church of the Holy Trinity]
Join Ben McNally Books, in partnership with Penguin Canada, for a special conversation with bestselling historian, novelist, and podcaster Dan Jones.
Dan will be discussing his new book
Castles: A Fortified History of the World
.
Doors will open at 6 p.m., the conversation will begin at 6:30. An audience Q & A will follow, and Dan will be happy to sign copies of his book at the end of the evening.
Two ticket options are available: General admission, and Book + Ticket. Book + Ticket includes a copy of Dan Jones' latest history,
Castles: A Fortified History of the World.
Please note:
neither ticket option will require a physical ticket, and you will not be charged for delivery if you choose any of the delivery options.
About the Book
From New York Times bestselling historian Dan Jones, a grand and sweeping history of the world, told through over three thousand years of iconic fortifications.
Castles have been built to defend humanity for millennia—from the walls of Troy in the Bronze Age and the desert bastion of Krak des Chevaliers in Syria; to Windsor Castle and the Tower of London; to Himeji in Japan and Fort Sumter in Charleston, South Carolina. They have inspired terror and passion, foiled conquering forces, and been deployed as the ultimate expression of wealth, status, and supremacy.
In
Castles
, Jones leads readers on a journey through the many eras of castle-building and across continents as each stronghold tells a unique story of power, politics, and survival, revealing the shifting tides of warfare, the rise and fall of empires, the resilience of people under siege, and the flourishing of new ideas.
Blending rich storytelling, deep research, and beautiful original illustrations,
Castles
is an epic story of why humans build fortifications and how they powerfully capture our imagination. With Jones's trademark scholarship and flair, he shows how defiance, endurance, and ambition have been carved into the landscapes we've inherited.
About the Author
Dan Jones is the
New York Times
bestselling author of
Henry V
,
Powers and Thrones
,
Crusaders
,
The Templars
,
The Plantagenets
,
Wars of the Roses
, and
Magna Carta
, as well as the
Essex Dogs
trilogy of novels.
He is the host of the podcast
This Is History: A Dynasty to Die For
and has produced, written, and presented dozens of TV shows, including the popular Netflix series Secrets of
Great British Castles
. As of 2025, he is a member of the board of trustees of Historic Royal Palaces, an organization dedicated to managing and maintaining the unoccupied palaces of England.

title: Discussing Treaties with Rick Monture
description:
Join Professor Rick Monture for a discussion about pre-contact peace agreements between Indigenous nations, treaties between Indigenous peoples and Europeans, and the various "numbered" treaties in Canada. Learn about the philosophies behind the Dish With One Spoon wampum and its significance today, as well as the 1784 Haldimand Proclamation as it pertains to First Nations in Southern Ontario. Come discover why treaties are a vital part of the movement towards Truth and Reconciliation!
No registration required.
Bio:
Rick Monture is a member of the Mohawk nation, Turtle clan, from Six Nations of the Grand River Territory.  He is a Professor in the Department of English & Cultural Studies and Indigenous Studies at McMaster University where he teaches classes on Indigenous literature, Haudenosaunee history, traditional narratives, and Bob Dylan.  He is also a Community Research Fellow with Six Nations Polytechnic and the Deyohahage / Indigenous Knowledge Centre based at Six Nations and is an active member of the language revitalization movement in his community.  In partnership with the Woodland Cultural Centre in Brantford, Rick currently holds a Social Science and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) award for a project that examines the events that led to the overthrow of the traditional Haudenosaunee government, by Ottawa, to implement an elected council system in 1924.  His book,
We Share our Matters: Two Centuries of Writing and Resistance at Six Nations of the Grand River
, was published in 2014 and is an examination of the Grand River Haudenosaunee’s assertions of sovereignty and social justice through letters, political activism, literature, and film. Rick lives at Six Nations with his family.
