title: The Way We Were: Seniors’ Memories of Life in the Junction
description:
Get a glimpse of the Junction in past decades through the memories and family stories of people who were there. Back Lane Studios, based in Roncesvalles, presents a selection of short videos from Mapping Our Memories, a project collecting place-based stories from older people in video and written formats. You'll learn about:
Sheila McIlraith's talented mother, a lively young woman who served as public health nurse at Annette and Runnymede public schools, drove her own car in the 1920s and was choir master and organist at High Park Baptist Church. But she gave all that up when she got married in her late 30s.
Local grocer Doug Breakwell, whose store was at the corner of Annette and Indian Grove Cres. He helped out Lorne Clayton's mother many times when she couldn't pay for groceries. But the tables turned. In the 1950s, when small stores were losing out to supermarkets, Lorne was able to help Doug out.
Lois Broad, who made our most popular video
Growing up in the Junction,
had many vivid memories to share, from the Minnies swimming pools at the corner of Quebec Ave. and Bloor, to High Park Avenue United Church, where her parents were the first couple to be married.
We'll screen a curated selection of short documentaries, learn about Mapping Our Memories, and meet some of the people behind the stories during a Q&A.
Light refreshments will be served.  Drop-in. No registration required.

title: ABCD Reads Body Language by Meg Howrey
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***[Body Language](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4801989)*** by Meg Howrey.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6325601387675648) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"Sloane, a former actress now working as a therapist, is determined to find a meaningful way through menopause, away from marketing schemes, possibly with the aid of psychedelics. Her sister Laurel is managing her own growing rage and restlessness while engaging in work at an environmental non-profit and raising teenagers. Nanette, the youngest, has answered a long-delayed religious calling and is living as a Novice in a convent. All three lives will be further disrupted when Sloane receives a call summoning her to their mother’s house, Laurel discovers possible evidence of her husband’s infidelity, and Nanette finds herself in the middle of a media frenzy after a spontaneous act of public prayer.
Soon, all three are reunited under their mother’s roof, and no one can seem to agree about anything beyond the Barbara has dementia, as did her mother and sister before her. Will it be an opportunity for the closed door of their very private mother’s inner life to crack open? A lesson in care; a shared responsibility that will be the making of this family, divided by large age gaps, parental divorce, and temperament? Or will a stunning revelation upend not only their mother’s remaining time, but divide the sisters permanently?
With razor-sharp prose and undeniable humor, acclaimed author Meg Howrey brings an American family in the midst of a painful crisis to unforgettable life, interrogating memory and emotional inheritance, the right of a woman’s autonomy, and the indelible bonds even the most disparate of sisters can share." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/244709885-body-language))

"Howrey is a reliably beautiful stylist, and her slyly funny prose and blade-sharp insights into human behavior really should put her in the same conversation as writers like Ann Patchett and Barbara Kingsolver. Though this novel hits some familiar beats, Howrey manages to haul in plenty of shimmering pearls on the perils and joys of womanhood—whatever that means.
A comfort meal of a novel: poignant and prismatic." (from [Kirkus](https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/meg-howrey/body-language-4/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). title: Civic Meetup #568: Hack the Count: Turning Window Sensors into Street Safety Evidence
description:
Topic: Hack the Count: Turning Window Sensors into Street Safety Evidence

When Ontario removed roughly 700 automated speed enforcement cameras from school and community safety zones in 2025, neighbourhoods lost one of their few sources of hard evidence about speeding. What happens when residents start collecting that evidence themselves?

This talk introduces CIVIC (Community-centred Infrastructures for Visible and Inclusive Cities), an urban living lab in London, Ontario. Residents host low-cost, privacy-by-design Telraam traffic sensors and noise monitors in their own windows. These sensors count cars, cyclists and pedestrians and estimate speeds, all without storing images. Professor Carrie Mitchell will walk through how the network was built, what the data shows, and how residents and city staff are using it to make the case for traffic calming. She’ll also cover what’s hard: data gaps, privacy trade-offs, and keeping a volunteer sensor network running. Finally, she’ll ask what it would take to scale community-owned street data across Ontario, and where civic technologists can help.

‎

Speaker: Carrie Mitchell (in-person)

Carrie Mitchell is an Associate Professor in the School of Planning at the University of Waterloo, where she studies urban climate resilience, community-based planning, and, more recently, road safety governance. She is the founder of CIVIC (OurCIVICFutures.ca), an urban living lab funded by Waterloo’s Global Futures Fund that is deploying privacy-by-design traffic and noise sensors with residents and community partners. Before joining Waterloo, she spent five years at Canada’s International Development Research Centre (IDRC) managing urban environment and climate research across Asia. She lives in London, Ontario.

‎

Agenda:

7:20-7:50 Presentation and Q\&A/discussion

Our weekly civic meetups bring together Torontonians (designers, coders, urban planners, government staff, mappers, policy-makers, students, communications strategists, community organizers, and more) who share an interest in making Toronto more responsive, prosperous, sustainable, and equitable through design, tech, and data.

description:
Date: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
Time: 7:00 pm to 9:00 pm (Doors open at 6:30 pm)

The Bata Shoe Museum is pleased to present the annual Founder’s Lecture, featuring special guest Charles Miers, Publisher and Editorial Director of Rizzoli imprints, in conversation with BSM Director and Senior Curator, Elizabeth Semmelhack, as they explore the intricate art of visual storytelling and the editorial vision behind some of the most celebrated fashion, design, and cultural books produced today.  
Renowned for creating some of the world’s most important and beautiful publications, Miers has shaped contemporary visual culture through publishing. Join us for an unforgettable evening as we discover: How does an editor decide which stories deserve a physical form? What transforms a collection of images and ideas into an iconic book? How does passion drive editorial direction? And how did Miers first enter the world of publishing, leading to a distinguished career at Rizzoli spanning over three decades?

title: Hot Docs & Soulpepper Present: Everybody to Kenmure Street
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
When the government came for their neighbours, an entire community stood in the way.

A new monthly series in partnership with Hot Docs, bringing visionary documentary filmmaking from around the world to Toronto’s East End.

From executive producer Emma Thompson comes an inspiring and profoundly moving portrait of what everyday citizens are capable of in the face of injustice. In May 2021, a U.K. Home Office dawn raid triggered one of the most spontaneous and successful acts of civil resistance in recent memory. In Scotland’s most diverse neighbourhood, hundreds of residents rush to the streets to stop the deportation of their neighbours. The morning in Glasgow, the first day of Eid, started as any other. But when neighbors heard through community message networks that two local men were snatched up for deportation, hundreds of people left their daily lives to rush down to Kenmure Street and put their bodies on the line. Though mostly strangers and with almost no planning, this extremely diverse group organized themselves, taking on essential roles to allow the collective to achieve their goal: protecting their own from government forces going after the most vulnerable among them. Everybody to Kenmure Street reminds us of the power that is always inherent in the people.

More information and registration can be found here: https://soulpepper.ca/everybody-to-kenmure-street/ https://soulpepper.ca/everybody-to-kenmure-street/ .

title: Toronto Railway Museum: From Harbour to Home: An Intro to Toronto’s Rail Lands
description:
Toronto’s Rail Lands once covered a massive swath of the city’s downtown with railway sidings, roundhouses, and maintenance spaces. Before that, the whole area was underwater, a harbour slowly filled in by the needs of the growing railway industry. Join the TRM’s Curator of Exhibits Dumaresq de Pencier as he explores the complex and layered history of the Railway Lands, from a bustling hive of activity during the golden age of rail to the modern commuter hub that more than 45,000 people call home. 
Dumaresq de Pencier is an award-winning museum researcher, television presenter, exhibit developer, and guide. He has had a lifelong interest in the history of vehicular technology. He is currently curator of both the Toronto Railway Museum and the Canadian Automotive Museum in Oshawa. In his spare time he enjoys rock climbing and writing tabletop roleplaying games. 
The Toronto Railway Museum hosts guest speakers online via the Zoom Webinar platform the Second Tuesday of each month. These talks are free and open to the public, with a suggested donation of $10 to support future programming. The Toronto Railway Museum is a registered Canadian charity (838626943RR0001) and charitable tax receipts will be issued for donations over $25.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons
location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

title: OCAD U X Reel Asian 2026
location: Off Campus Marina Quay West, 539 Queens Quay West
description:
The 2026 edition of Reel Asian celebrates the 30th anniversary of the festival. In-person programming runs from Nov 11. to 21 with events across Toronto, including at OCAD University. Online events will take place from Nov. 16 to 29.

The Toronto Reel Asian International Film Festival ® is a unique showcase of contemporary cinema and works by Asia, Asian diaspora, and Asian Canadian filmmakers and creatives. Works include films and videos by Asian-identifying artists in Canada, the U.S., Asia and all over the world. As Canada’s largest pan-Asian film festival, Reel Asian ® provides a public forum for Asian media artists and their work, and fuels the growing appreciation for Asian cinema in Canada. The 2026 edition of Reel Asian celebrates the 30th anniversary of the festival. In-person programming runs from Nov 11. to 21 with events across Toronto, including at OCAD University. Online events will take place from Nov. 16 to 29. This year, OCAD U is pleased to host a variety of exhibitions and virtual reality projects as part of the festival. Visit reelasian.com/festival for more info. Tickets on sale now! Use the code REELASIAN30 for 15% off tickets.

Palace Immersive Goong (이머시브궁) (Nov. 12 to 21)

Join a multi-user VR journey set in Korea's iconic Gyeongbokgung Palace, where the grandeur of the Joseon Dynasty’s last unrealized royal banquet comes to life. More than a spectator, you are a part of the celebration in this cutting-edge, location-based entertainment experience that seamlessly blends history, culture, and technology in real time. Location : Open Space Gallery, 49 McCaul St., OCAD University Dates : Nov. 12 to 21, 12 to 5 p.m. Tickets : Pay what you can

Means to Enfold (Nov. 13 to 19)

Means to Enfold is an embrace, a remembrance, and a suggestion towards the ways we hold each other together through collective expression. In bringing together interactive installations, a travelling exhibit of works developed at the SSX x InterAccess AR residency, a curated section of student works created in Tech Jams and invited artworks by artists part of the inaugural SSX Artist Residency, this community showcase highlights how collaboration can be a potent means to enfold the meanings in all our relations. Drop by for the Means to Enfold opening reception on Friday, Nov. 13 from 7:30 to 11 p.m., featuring live music and refreshments. Bring your infectious energies to the SSX Sing-Along Karaoketo to end the evening at a high note. All singing styles and music genres welcome! Location : Open Space Gallery, 49 McCaul St., OCAD University Dates : Nov. 13 to Nov 19, 12 to 5 p.m. Tickets : Free

Expanded Dis/Closures Fireside Chat: Ana Serrano & Romeo Candido (Nov. 13)

OCAD U President and Vice-Chancellor Ana Serrano (left) and director, writer and composer Romeo Candido (right). Join this fireside chat with Ana Serrano, president and vice-chancellor of OCAD University and recipient of Reel Asian's 2026 Fire Horse Award, and Romeo Candido, Emmy-nominated director, writer, composer, and Canadian Screen Award-winning producer working across film, television, theatre, and music. They will open the Expanded Dis/Closures exhibition and conference with this fireside chat discussing ever-changing media and the role of creators in the challenges of our time. The fireside chat will be followed by the Sari-Sari Reception at 7 p.m. Location : OCAD University Auditorium, 100McCaul St., OCAD University Dates : Nov. 13, 7 p.m. Tickets : Free

Expanded Dis/Closures - XR Summit (Nov. 16)

Reel Asian’s XR Summit is a space for dialogue between emerging and established artists and studios, professionals from the industry, media scholars and the wider communities who will connect and explore the state of the creative industries and the market trends leading innovation within the domains of XR and spatial media, both globally and locally. Location : School of Graduate Studies, 205 Richmond St. W., OCAD University Dates : Nov. 16, 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tickets : Free

title: Nov 11 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Time, Date and Location**

Nov 11, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-november-11-2026)**

**Agentic RAG: Beyond Retrieve-and-Generate**

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the default pattern for grounding large language models in external knowledge, but most implementations still follow a rigid retrieve-once, generate-once pipeline — one that struggles with multi-hop questions, ambiguous queries, and knowing when its own retrieved context is insufficient. This talk introduces Agentic RAG, where retrieval is treated as an action within an agent's reasoning loop rather than a fixed upstream step.

We'll examine query decomposition and routing for breaking complex questions into targeted sub-queries, self-reflective and corrective retrieval loops that let an agent judge and re-query its own results, and tool-orchestration patterns (via MCP) that let retrieval sit alongside other agent actions like database lookups and API calls. Using a live architecture — evolving a standard RAG chatbot into an agentic, MCP-connected system — we'll walk through what changes in design, and where these systems introduce new failure modes: grounding drift, latency and cost from repeated retrieval loops, and cases where a simpler RAG pipeline still wins.

Attendees will leave with a practical framework for deciding when the added complexity of agentic RAG is worth it, and a set of design patterns for building it correctly.

*About the Speaker*

[Balaji Venkatasubramaniyar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/balaji-venkatasubramaniyar/) is a Technical Lead at Wisdom Infotech, leading a 15+ person engineering team delivering enterprise solutions. With 13+ years of experience in enterprise software and insurance technology, he specializes in agentic AI systems, RAG architectures, and vector databases.

**GeoAI for the Physical World: Earth Observation, Foundation Models, and Urban Digital Twins**

Earth observation provides a unique form of computer vision for understanding the physical world at city to continental scales. In this talk, I will show how satellite imagery, geospatial data, machine learning, and foundation-model representations can be combined to characterize urban environments and environmental conditions.

I will present UrbanScope Open, an open GeoAI digital-twin prototype integrating Earth observation with 3D buildings, vegetation, land-surface temperature, air quality, noise, population, and other urban data. I will also share lessons from my research using geospatial foundation-model embeddings for environmental prediction across Europe.

The talk will discuss how these approaches can contribute to increasingly multimodal AI systems capable of reasoning about real-world environments.

*About the Speaker*

[Cesar Alvarez](https://voxel51.com/events/cesar.alvarez@uni-a.de) is a researcher at the University of Augsburg working at the intersection of GeoAI, Earth observation, remote sensing, and environmental intelligence. His research applies machine learning, computer vision, and geospatial foundation models to problems including urban environments, climate risk, air quality, and agriculture.

**Can agents get curious?**

Most AI agents are good at answering a question once we tell them exactly what to look for. The harder problem is building agents that can explore a complex dataset autonomously: generating hypotheses, deciding which analyses are worth running, allocating additional compute when evidence is ambiguous, and knowing when they have enough evidence to stop.

In this talk, I’ll show an architecture for autonomous research agents that combines structured knowledge, iterative tool use, and explicit evidence tracking to turn open-ended questions into a sequence of testable investigations. I’ll discuss practical lessons from building and evaluating these systems, including why more test-time compute does not automatically produce better research and how provenance and evaluation can make long-running agents more reliable.

I’ll close with a live example of an agent exploring a dataset, revising its hypotheses, and choosing what to investigate next.

*About the Speaker*

[Srivatsa P](https://www.linkedin.com/in/srivatsa-p) is a member of technical staff at Sigma Computing, where he works on AI agents that reason over complex enterprise data. Previously, he worked on machine learning at Apple and conducted research at the MIT Media Lab; outside of traditional ML, he has also worked on mapping coral reefs through underwater imaging, which sparked an enduring interest in how intelligent systems make sense of messy real-world data.

**Does Cross-Validation Work in Deep Learning?**

Cross-validation is a standard in hyperparameter optimization in classical ML, but is generally considered computationally prohibitive and unnecessary in deep learning. We investigated whether CV produces 1. better DL models 2. better estimates of future performance of said models. We focused on medical image classification as an important deep learning application domain.

Our results show that cross-validation consistently and materially reduces the gap between development and independent testing error for relatively small training datasets (up to about 1000 images). The test performance improvement was generally modest. We discuss the implications for deep-learning practitioners, including whether the increased computational cost of cross-validation is justified.

*About the Speaker*

[Ljubomir Buturovic](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ljubomir-buturovic-798156/) is an AI scientist and biotech executive with extensive experience in clinical diagnostics, including work at Inflammatix and Pathwork Diagnostics. His current research focuses on deep-learning image classification, infectious disease adjudication using LLMs, and development of AI models for helping critically ill patients.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Fridays to Sundays 1 to 5 pm

title: Nov 11 - Toronto Physical AI Workshop and Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join us at the University of Toronto on November 11 for the Toronto Physical AI Workshop and Meetup, co-presented by Nebius and Voxel51.

Seats are limited, **[Pre-registration is mandatory.](https://voxel51.com/events/toronto-physical-ai-workshop-and-meetup-november-11-2026)**

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 11, 2026
5:30 PM - 8:30 PM
The Conference Centre at U of T
Giovanni Room (2nd Floor)
89 Chestnut St.
Toronto, ON M5G 1R1

**Meetup Agenda**
*5:30–6:30 PM*

* Networking, food, drinks, and lightning talks

**Workshop Agenda**
This hands-on session uses DROID, a real-world robotics dataset loaded into FiftyOne as a native multimodal MCAP recording, and YOLO11n, fine-tuned live during the session.

*6:30–7:30 PM*

* Welcome + framing: from raw robot logs to a trained detector
* Explore a real DROID robotics recording in FiftyOne's native multimodal MCAP viewer: camera, proprioception, and language on one synced timeline, no ROS install required
* Curate: extract and browse frames from the recording, filter and deduplicate
* Compute embeddings on the curated frames; explore via similarity search and embeddings visualization (via Nebius Serverless AI Jobs)

*7:30–8:00 PM*

* Auto-label: open-vocabulary detection to generate bounding boxes for the robot gripper and target objects
* Train: fine-tune a YOLO11n detector on the auto-labeled frames (via Nebius Serverless AI Jobs)
* Evaluate results and close the loop: view predictions back on the original MCAP timeline

*8:00–8:30 PM*

* What else Nebius offers: Token Factory walkthrough — chat/vision models, fine-tuning, credits

title: The Writings of David Thompson on His Travels in North America
location: North York Central Library, Room 1, 2nd floor
description:
The Writings of David Thompson
This presentation examines the historical Writings of David Thompson. Between 1784 and 1812, David Thompson (1770-1857) explored and traded over a vast expanse of western North America. Later in life, the surveyor and fur trader wrote what he called his
Travels
, a spectacular geographical and spirited intellectual journey of the Canadian experience. His story tells of a remarkable life in the fur trade but it also captures hid reflections on the land and the indigenous peoples of western North America.
Presented by Bill Moreau, editor of the three-volume work,
The Writings of David Thompson
.
Registration is encouraged but not necessary.

title: 'Hunger' at the Alumnae Theatre (Nov 11 to Nov 22)
location: Alumnae Theatre,70 Berkeley St, Toronto, ON M5A 2W5, Canada
description:
ALUMNAE THEATRE OPENS ALL-CANADIAN, ALL-FEMALE PLAYWRIGHT SEASON WITH MEGHAN GREELEY’S HUNGER

Alumnae Theatre is proud to launch its 2026/2027 season, centred around the theme Stories of Survival, with Newfoundland playwright Meghan Greeley’s riveting drama, Hunger. Directed by Sarini Kumarasinghe and produced by Kimberley Ann Croscup, the production runs from November 11 to November 22, 2026, in the Studio Theatre.

Hunger marks the opening production in a milestone season for Alumnae Theatre, featuring a lineup written entirely by Canadian female playwrights.

Set in an isolated farmhouse during an unspecified period of war, Hunger explores survival, currency, and the fragile nature of morality. In the midst of a violent conflict, Johanna and Max attempt an act of heroics by hiding three refugees in a tiny alcove behind their walls. As space and food dwindle and the war outside reaches a deafening climax, the couple and their secret guests are pushed to their absolute limits.

First premiered by Newfoundland’s White Rooster Theatre in 2019 before embarking on a provincial tour, Greeley’s play earned widespread critical acclaim upon its publication by Breakwater Books, where it was named a finalist for the prestigious BMO Winterset Award. Praised by literary reviewers for its "askew dialogue and cutaway violence" reminiscent of the haunting, surrealist works of Caryl Churchill, Hunger delivers a tense, dark examination of human nature under extreme duress.

"We’re thrilled to begin our season with a play that so fiercely challenges our understanding of human endurance and compassion," says the production team. "Greeley's voice sets a fitting tone for a season dedicated to extraordinary stories of survival written by some of Canada’s most compelling female theatre artists."

The cast is led by Yolande Williams and Ryan Giesen (as Johanna and Max) with Kimberly Van Vo, Arya Ashoori, and Irene Kalogridis (as Rivka, Isaac, and Helen) filling out this ensemble of striking local talent.

“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

Get your tickets today https://soulpepper.ca/whats-on/de-profundis-oscar-wilde-in-jail/ !

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

title: Unsettling the Public Record: Decolonial Research Methods for Troubling Times
description:
As censorship and retaliation become growing concerns, turning to public records and events as sources of ethnographic data raises important ethical questions. Guided by Black feminist critiques of archival violence, Alexandra will examine how the very idea of what is considered “public” can reproduce harm and shape the people and communities represented within public records.
The session will explore the situated ethical obligations that emerge when conducting ethnographic research in and through publics, and consider how research practices can not only unsettle the public record, but contribute to building more just worlds in troubling times.
Participants are welcome to attend all three sessions. Zoom details will be shared with registered participants ahead of each workshop.

title: Common Hour: Celebrating the Canadian League of Composers: John Burge, Piano
location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall, 112 Accolade East Building, York University
description:
In celebration of the Canadian League of Composers 75th Anniversary in 2026, composer and pianist, John Burge presents a solo piano recital of music composed by many of the CLC past presidents. Starting with music by founding President, John Weinzweig, the program proceeds chronologically to current president, Tyler Versluis. The concert opens with a musical land acknowledgement, “Trillium,” composed by Indigenous-Canadian composer and CLC member, Beverley McKiver, and concludes with a rousing collective singing of O Canada. This all-Canadian concert promises to be an event of historical, cultural and artistic significance.
Thursday, November 12, 2026
12:30 – 1:30 p.m. 
Tribute Communities Recital Hall
FREE
Composer and pianist, John Burge ( https://sdm.queensu.ca/people/burge-john ), taught at Queen’s University, Kingston, Ontario, for 38 years before retiring as a Professor Emeritus in 2025. Many of Burge’s orchestral works, such as Snowdrift, The Canadian Shield and Rocky Mountain Overture, have been performed by orchestras across Canada and internationally. His string orchestra work, Flanders Fields Reflections, as recorded by Sinfonia Toronto, received the 2009 Juno Award for the Best Canadian Classical Composition. In 2014 he was inducted into the Royal Society of Canada for his achievements as a composer and support of the Arts in Canada. Having completed his Associate Diploma from the Royal Conservatory of Toronto in Piano Performance while still in high school, John Burge has continued to perform throughout his career, usually in presentations of his own music. Over the years, his piano music has been included in a number of conservatory music syllabi and he is in high demand as a music festival adjudicator. A passionate advocate for Canadian music, he served on the executive committee of the Canadian League of Composers from 1993-2007 (including eight years as President) and on the SOCAN Foundation board of directors from 2009-2025, as well as on the boards of several arts organizations in the Kingston area.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.

Penguins: The Adventures of Pimba and family
description:
Discover more about penguin biology, ecology, and migration in this presentation of a collection of photographs taken during an MSc research exchange at the Punta Tombo Penguin Reserve in Patagonia, Argentina.
The photographs are accompanied by the story of Pimba, a penguin who migrates with her family from Patagonia to Brazil by following ocean currents. Through Pimba’s journey, children are introduced to the penguin life cycle in an engaging and accessible way, using real scientific research brought to life through storytelling and images.

title: From Agentic Development to Automated Delivery
description:
Toronto Enterprise DevOps User Group
How do you move from actively guiding AI agents to having them carry work through your team’s development process?

Join us for a practical session on agentic workflows in GitHub. We’ll show how people and agents clarify requirements, plan changes, and capture project knowledge, then use those shared skills and context to automate tasks such as assessing issues and reviewing pull requests.

Through demos, we’ll explore how these steps can connect into a workflow that takes a small bug from report to proposed fix, helping teams move faster and reduce bottlenecks. Along the way, we’ll show how engineers can inspect the agent’s work, step in when it needs refinement, and retain control over what merges.

*Come at 5:30 PM to grab some pizza and network. The presentation kicks off at 6:00 PM!*

Surtout, il sait ce qu'on lui doit, même si ce n'est pas justifié, et qu'on l'aime encore, qu'on l'aimera toujours.

title: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark
location: Lillian H. Smith, Lower Level- Auditorium
description:
Photo credit: Lee Higginson.
Join the Osborne Collection of Early Children's Books for our 19th Annual Sybille Pantazzi Memorial Lecture: Imagining a Turtle Named Franklin by Brenda Clark.
Award winning picture book illustrator, Brenda Clark is the original illustrator of the beloved Franklin the Turtle book series, by author Paulette Bourgeois. In this lecture, she will share how she became an artist and how Franklin was created. Brenda’s illustrations have played a key role in Franklin’s worldwide popularity, leading to the inspiration of the animated TV series, merchandise, spin-off books, a children’s garden on Toronto Island and a Canadian postage stamp. She will walk us through the process of designing and painting the art and explain how it takes some amazing teamwork to meet the challenges of Franklin’s success.
For the past 40 years, Brenda Clark has delighted children as the illustrator of the hugely successful Franklin the Turtle children’s book series. Over 70 million Franklin books have been sold in more than 30 languages worldwide, making it the single most successful picture book series in the history of Canadian publishing. In 2011, the archives of Brenda Clark were donated to the Osborne Collection of Early Children’s Books, and recognized by the Canadian Cultural Property Export Review Board as cultural property for its “Outstanding Significance and National Importance”. In 2014, Brenda was named a Member of the Order of Canada. She lives in Port Hope, Ontario.
Book signings will take place before the lecture from 5:00-6:00 pm on the 4th floor in the Osborne Collection.
Franklin in the Dark

This session introduces public data sources like the Toronto Open Data Portal and Kaggle, then shows you how AI tools can help you explore and analyze that data without any technical background. You will learn how to find datasets relevant to a civic issue, ask AI the right questions to surface insights, and turn raw numbers into something meaningful. No experience required.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Radiant Vermin presented by Riot King Art Market
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen St E, Toronto, M4M 2J5
description:
Riot King is back on stage this November with Radiant Vermin by playwright Philip Ridley, playing November 12th to the 22nd. 
Celebrated indie theatre company Riot King Art Market is back on stage this November with Radiant Vermin by playwright Philip Ridley, playing November 12th to the 22nd, 2026 at The Red Sandcastle Theatre in Toronto’s beautiful East End. 
Ollie and Jill want to tell you about their dream home. Some of the things they did to get it, you might find shocking. But they want you to know they did it all for their baby… 
Radiant Vermin is a wickedly comedic satire about a young couple who are offered a way onto the property ladder that may turn out to be too good to be true. Through a whirlwind retelling of everything they’ve done to get their dream home, Ollie and Jill show us just how far we might go to build a better life for ourselves. Playful, provocative, and viciously sharp, this outrageous dark comedy comments on the housing crisis, homelessness, and what it really takes to support a family in today’s world. It will leave Toronto audiences shocked, thrilled, and feeling a little more connected to everyone who calls this city home. 
Content Advisory: Strong language, mature themes, discussions of violence. 
Run time: 110 minutes no intermission. There will be no re-entry.

location: The Assembly Theatre,1479 Queen Street West, Toronto, ON M6R 1A1, Canada
description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

Directed by Bonnie Duff (Assistant Director Jane Austen’s Northanger Abbey, Guild Festival Theatre; Playwright/Performer This Feels Like The End, Theatre Aurinko/Next Stage Festival) and starring Lara Lucia (The Drowsy Chaperone, Shifting Ground Collective; Brontë: The World Without, Guild Festival Theatre) and Jack Copland (The Moors, Riot King Theatre; The Comeback, Globus Theatre), Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons features Scenic Design by Kenzia Dalie (Panoply Collective; Full House Productions), Lighting Design by Jay Hines (Crow’s Theatre; Shifting Ground Collective), and Sound Design by Jake Schindler (Mixtape Productions; Second City; Stratford Festival).

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.
Some Experience with GenAI Recommended: This course is ideal for participants who have completed the AI Essentials course Learning Circle.
How to Joi
n a Learning Circle:
Register once for the first session of this event series, in order to attend all sessions.
Please sign up with a valid email address.
A valid TPL library card is required for online circles.
Attend all four sessions online via Zoom, Fridays, November 6, 13, 20, and 27, from 9:30 AM-12 PM.

description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: CANCELLED - Continental Philosophy Research Group (Dimitris Vardoulakis, Western Sydney University)
location: Factor-Inwentash Faculty of Social Work, 246 Bloor Street West, Room 620, Toronto, ON, M5S 1V4, Canada
description:
This talk has unfortunately been cancelled. 
The Continental Philosophy Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Dimitris Vardoulakis, who was the inaugural chair of Philosophy at Western Sydney University. Some of his books include Spinoza, the Epicurean: Authority and Utility in Materialism (2020); The Ruse of Techne: Heidegger’s Magical Materialism (2024); The Agonistic Condition: Materialism and Democracy (2025); and The Logic of Living: The Materialism of Ancient Greek Thought (forthcoming). He is the co-editor of the book series “Incitements” (Edinburgh University Press) and the journal Philosophy, Politics and Critique. He is currently Vice President of the Council of the Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences (CHASS) and has served as chair of the Australasian Society for Continental Philosophy (ASCP). 
Title
What is Materialism? 
Abstract
If we reflect on the use of the word “materialism,” we will be confounded by its diverse and even contradictory meanings: It can refer both to the “material girl” as the embodied subject of high capitalism and neoliberalism, and to the historical materialist dialectic of Marx, or Marxism. It describes both Spinoza’s equation of god and nature that leads to a radical politics, and the naturalist principle that everything is subject to causality and hence scientifically understandable, which seems to lack a politics altogether. 
In this presentation, I will argue that how we understand the history of materialism affects what we understand by this term. To present this position, I will synthesize insights from four books on the history and politics of materialism that I have published since 2020. The upshot will be the argument that materialism is a much more powerful analytic concept in politics than it has been recognized hitherto.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Séances & The World Wars
description:
Séances were all the rage a century ago. Having begun to fall out of fashion in the early 1900s, they experienced a resurgence after the deadly years of the First World War and the Spanish Flu as people held out hope they could still communicate with their lost loved ones. In the third lecture of this series by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore the history of séances during those turbulent times, from those who truly believed in their power, to the fraudsters who preyed on a grieving city, to the prime minister who took advice from the spirits of the dead.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

title: Like a Bird's Nest
location: Pix Film Gallery,1411 Dufferin St Unit B, Toronto, ON M6H 4C7, Canada
description:
Sala-Manca Group (Lea Mauas and Diego Rotman) in collaboration with Meydad Eliyahu, Brian Hoad, Ktura Manor, Itamar Mendes-Flohr, Yeshaiahu Rabinowitz, and Nir Yahalom

FENTSTER is pleased to present a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group https://sala-manca.net/sala-manca-group . Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah—a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation.

This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

Experience three full-size sukkah structures including a new outdoor commission from local artists: Maxine Lee Ewaschuk, Rochelle Rubinstein, and Jessica Thalmann. Thalmann also debuts a window installation at the host venue, PIX FILM Gallery, that is on view 24/7.

Presented by FENTSTER http://fentster.org/ in collaboration with venue partner PIX FILM Gallery https://www.pixfilm.ca/

description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🎶 Niagara Falls Concert Road Trip: Roch Voisine at OLG Stage!

**Friday, November 13, 2026**
Ready for a night of great music and a little Niagara Falls adventure? Join us for a road trip from Toronto to see **Roch Voisine – The Lightfoot Sessions Live** at the **OLG Stage at Fallsview Casino**! 🎤🎶

### 🎵 The Concert

Roch Voisine brings **The Lightfoot Sessions Live** to Niagara Falls for a special evening celebrating his incredible career and the music of Canadian legend **Gordon Lightfoot**.
Voisine is one of Canada's best-known singer-songwriters, with a career spanning four decades and 25 albums. His massive breakthrough came with *Hélène*, which went triple platinum in Canada and diamond in France.
The show will feature Roch's greatest hits along with his tribute to Gordon Lightfoot. 🇨🇦🎶
**Concert:** Roch Voisine – The Lightfoot Sessions Live
**Date:** Friday, November 13, 2026
**Venue:** OLG Stage at Fallsview Casino
**Showtime:** 8:00 PM

### 🚗 The Road Trip

We'll meet **outside Christie Station at 4:30 PM** and head to Niagara Falls in a **Kia Soul with SiriusXM radio**.
Depending on traffic and how the evening is going, we may have some time to **sightsee around Niagara Falls before the concert**. 🌊📸
After the show, we'll head back to Toronto.
**Expected return to Toronto: around 11:30 PM**, depending on traffic and the timing of the evening.

**$50 includes:**

* 🎟️ Your concert ticket
* 🚗 Round-trip transportation from Toronto
* ⛽ Transportation costs

That's it — **just $50 for the concert AND the ride!**

nicolasbello@yahoo.com

description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
🎬 Let’s Go to the Movies (and Actually Talk… or Not)

Whether you're a film nerd, popcorn enthusiast, or just looking for a chill night out with interesting people — this one's for you.

We’re heading out to see a movie together, then grabbing food or drinks after. If the film's great (or terrible), we’ll probably talk about it forever. If it’s just okay, we’ll talk about it for 10 minutes and move on to everything else — books, dating apps, weird dreams, how Toronto keeps getting more expensive, etc.

The vibe is relaxed, friendly, and not too serious. No film degree needed. No icebreakers. No pressure to “perform.” Just come enjoy the film, connect with some thoughtful people, and see where the night goes Click here to watch trailer!

🎞️ **Movie Title + Trailer:** [\[Click here to watch trailer!\]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ORxw68y3lyw)

📖 **📖 Plot Summary:** A crew of social media-savvy bank robbers broadcasts their daring heists, unaware that their growing viral fame has put them in the crosshairs of a veteran FBI agent and a brilliant software engineer. Despite the unlikely duo closing in on the crew, the crime syndicate pushes past their limits, putting everything on the line for their beliefs — and their most ambitious heist yet.

***

### 🗓️ **Event Details**

📍 **Meetup Time:** 6:00 PM (Final time + theatre announced Tuesday of event week)
🎬 **Movie Start Time:** TBA

* **$11.50** for *CineClub* members
* **$16.00** regular admission
👉 You are responsible for buying your own ticket.

**🪑 Reserved Seating:**
You must buy your ticket *before* signing up. You'll be asked where you're sitting so we can all sit together! However, members are welcome to sit anywhere that works for them.
🎫 Buy your ticket here: [https://www.cineplex.com](https://www.cineplex.com)
📍🪑 **Where I will be sitting:**

🍿 **After the Movie:**
Yes, we’re heading out after! It’s not just a movie night — it’s a social night. Let's talk, laugh, and dissect every plot twist.

***

### ✅ **Before You Sign Up**

* Please **buy your ticket first** — seating is limited!
* When signing up, let us know your **seat number** so we can try to group everyone together.
* You can still sign up or just **show up on the day** if you’re not sure you can make it — we’re flexible!

***

### 🎥 **A Quick Word About Movie Etiquette**

We love a great film experience. Please:

* Turn off your phone
* Don’t talk during the movie
* Be respectful of others

Repeat offenders will be removed from the group — we take our cinema seriously (but with snacks).

***

This event is open to everyone — single, not single, shy, social, new in town or a long-time local. We're a group for people who love movies *and* making real connections. We also do walks, hikes, restaurants, arts & culture — come be part of it!

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

Get your tickets today https://soulpepper.ca/whats-on/de-profundis-oscar-wilde-in-jail/ !

Over the last four decades, Béla Fleck has made a point of boldly going where no banjo player has gone before, a musical journey that has earned him 19 Grammys in nine different fields, including country, pop, jazz, instrumental, classical, and global music.

But his roots are in bluegrass, and that is where he returns with his band of all-star players, My Bluegrass Heart.

https://www.belafleck.com/

Taking its namesake from Fleck's 2021 Grammy Award-winning album, *My Bluegrass Heart*, the album was the third chapter of a trilogy which began with the 1988 album, *Drive*, and continued in 1991 with The Bluegrass Sessions. Fleck’s band spotlights a multi-generational gamut of the best of bluegrass players, all sporting a myriad of Grammy nominations, as well as gigantic piles of IBMA awards for their instruments: fiddler Michael Cleveland, mandolinist Dominick Leslie, Jeff Partin on dobro, bassist/multi-instrumentalist Mark Schatz, and Jake Stargel on guitar.

description:
What would you say if you had only 140 words a day?

Discover Sam Steiner's play this November.

Presented at The Assembly Theatre in November 2026, Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons is part rom-com, part sci-fi, and part dystopian drama.

The average person will speak 123,205,750 words in a lifetime. But what if there were a limit? Oliver and Bernadette are about to find out. Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons Lemons imagines a world where we’re forced to say less. It’s about what we say and how we say it; about the things we can only hear in the silence; about dead cats, activism, eye contact and lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons, lemons.

title: Intro to Survival Skills: Shelter, Fire and Knots
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/survival-skills/intro-survival-skills)**
**Spend a Saturday becoming someone who knows what to do.**
Join us for a hands-on beginner day in Copeland Forest with Kyle, a survival instructor with over a decade of experience. You'll pitch a shelter, light a fire without matches, carve with a knife and tie the knots that hold it all together.
This class is open to any adult, member or not. Come on your own or bring a friend. Most people at our classes arrive solo. Total beginners are welcome: Kyle starts from zero, and there's no hiking, just short walks into the trees to gather wood.
**Kit provided:** Tarps, saws, hatchets, loaner ferro rods and knives to borrow, plus your own tinder kit and a printed handout. Want your own ferro rod (+$10) or Mora knife (+$40) to keep? Add one when you book.
**Getting there:** Add the bus for $50 and we'll pick you up at Keele Station at 8am and drop you back around 6pm. Or drive yourself to the P1 parking lot in Copeland Forest, near Horseshoe Valley, about an hour and a half north of Toronto.
No membership needed. After you book, we'll email you the waiver to sign and your plan with directions, timings and a packing list.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Put a roof over your head:** Learn to pick a good spot and pitch a tarp two ways, the A-frame and the plow point, so you know how to stay dry when the weather turns.
**Light a fire without matches:** Catch a ferro rod spark on fluffed jute, build up through twigs to logs, split wood by batoning and carve feather sticks.
**Knots, knife work and a tripod grill:** Learn the taut-line hitch, slip knot and bowline, carve your own chopsticks, spoon or spatula, then lash a tripod and grill over the fire.
**Itinerary**
**08:00** \- Bus leaves Keele Station \(if you've added it\)
**10:00** \- Meet at location\, for a welcome\, safety talk and knife handling
**Late morning** \- Tarp shelters: the A\-frame and the plow point
**Lunch** \- Bring a packed lunch and eat around the fire
**Afternoon** \- Fire without matches: ferro rod\, jute\, batoning and feather sticks
**Late afternoon** \- Knots\, bush cutlery and a tripod grill
**16:00** \- Wrap up and head home
**18:00** \- Bus arrives back at Keele Station
**Event cost: $135+HST. $50 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/survival-skills/intro-survival-skills)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: 🍁🎄Fall Niagara Falls Hiking Day Trip — Trails, Dinner & Festival of Lights!!
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍁🎄 Niagara Falls Fall Hiking Trip & Winter Festival of Lights! 🌈

🌦️ **RAIN OR SHINE!**

The adventure goes on, whether we're enjoying golden sunshine, crisp autumn air, or a little mist from the Falls. After a day of hiking, we'll finish with dinner and the spectacular Winter Festival of Lights! ✨

***

## 🥾 About the Trip

Let's escape the city for a full day of fresh air, friendship, and breathtaking scenery! We'll explore the natural side of Niagara Falls — less time in the tourist crowds, more trails, trees, and spectacular views.

We'll meet outside the **Fairmont Royal York on Front Street West**, travel together by GO Train to Niagara Falls, and make our way to **Niagara Glen Nature Reserve** for a hike among ancient boulders, winding forest paths, and the turquoise waters of the Niagara River.

The trail features stairs, uneven ground, elevation changes, and a climb back up out of the gorge. This is a proper hike, so please read the expectations below before signing up.

**A Special Guest Joining Us!**

We're excited to welcome Miles Howard, visiting us from Boston on November 14–15!

Miles is writing *HIKE EVERY CITY*, a book (coming in 2028) exploring urban hiking, community, and how exploring cities on foot brings people together. He also runs a similar urban hiking project in Boston called *Walking City Trails*.

He'll be joining us for both weekend outings, including Niagara Falls, to experience our group firsthand and meet our members.
Feel free to say hello, share your experiences, and chat with Miles if you'd like. No pressure, of course!

It's exciting to see our community getting noticed beyond Toronto. Let's give Miles a warm welcome!

***

## 🌲 The Trail Experience

Niagara Glen is a beautiful natural area carved into the Niagara Gorge over thousands of years. We'll follow forest trails, take photos, enjoy the fall colours, and experience a side of Niagara Falls that many visitors never see.

The planned hike is approximately **4 km**, although the terrain makes it more demanding than the distance might suggest. We'll have opportunities to pause and enjoy the scenery, but everyone needs to be prepared for the physical demands of the route.

### ⚠️🥾 IMPORTANT: HIKE EXPECTATIONS — PLEASE READ CAREFULLY 🥾⚠️

**This is a real hiking trail, not a casual walk.**
Before signing up, please be confident that you can:

* ✔️ Walk for an extended period of time.
* ✔️ Handle uneven terrain, stairs, elevation changes, and the climb back up out of the gorge.
* ✔️ Keep up with the group at a steady pace without needing frequent or extended stops.
* ✔️ Manage a full day of walking, travel, dinner, and evening sightseeing.

**This is not the event to use to test your fitness level or see how things go.** If you're unsure whether you can complete the hike, please choose an easier event instead.
If you find yourself unable to keep up, you may need to turn back or continue independently where the route and circumstances allow.

The group cannot stop or slow down significantly to accommodate someone who is struggling, as this affects the experience and schedule for everyone.
Please make an honest assessment of your abilities before committing. The goal is to keep the day safe, enjoyable, and on track for the entire group.

***

## 🍔 Dinner at Chuck's Roadhouse

After the hike, we'll head to **Chuck's Roadhouse on Clifton Hill** for a relaxed dinner. Everyone is responsible for the cost of their own meal.

⚠️ **Please note:** The restaurant has limited vegetarian options. If this means you won't be joining us for dinner, please let me know in advance so I can plan the numbers. Please don't leave this until the last minute, as I'll be arranging the dinner headcount.

***

## 🎇 Winter Festival of Lights

After dinner, we'll head down to the Falls to enjoy the **Niagara Falls Winter Festival of Lights**.
The surrounding area comes alive with illuminated displays and colourful seasonal installations. We'll take a relaxed evening stroll, enjoy the atmosphere, and stop for photos along the way.
Bring warm layers — temperatures near the Falls can drop, especially after dark! 🧣✨

title: York Circle Lecture Series
description:
Don’t miss out on the chance to hear from some of York’s leading faculty members on a wide range of fascinating topics at our next York Circle session. Connect with other alumni, gain valuable insights from our featured professors, and ask your own questions on important topics.
Date: Saturday, Nov. 14
Time: 9 a.m. – 1 p.m.
Location: Life Sciences Building, Keele Campus
Tickets: $5 includes coffee, light snacks and lunch.

Attendees will have the opportunity to choose one lecture from each session during the registration process.
First sessions – 10 a.m. 

Diagnostic and Prognostic Medical Devices: From research to real-world impact
Presented by Neda Salahandish, Assistant Professor, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and Biomedical Engineering, Lassonde School of Engineering, and CEO, WearDOXX
Drawing on examples from her research, Dr. Salahandish will discuss the development of diagnostic and prognostic medical devices, including electrochemical biosensors, microfluidic point-of-care technologies, wearable devices, and AI-enabled health platforms.

AI at the Dentist’s Chair: Transforming periodontal disease detection with DePERIO
Presented by Ebrahim Ghafar-Zadeh, Associate Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Gum disease is one of the most common oral health conditions, yet early detection can be challenging and often depends on specialized clinical assessment. This talk will introduce DePERIO, an AI-enabled portable technology developed to support rapid and accessible assessment of periodontal health.

Second Sessions – 11:20 a.m.

Microchips Meet Mind: Tiny electronics that listen to, and heal, the brain
Presented by Hossein Kassiri, Associate Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Lassonde School of Engineering
Professor Hossein Kassiri will share how his lab will bring hospital-quality brain monitoring into a comfortable headband through a tiny, wireless devices that detects epileptic seizures and stops them before they spread. This innovation could one day restore sight to people with retinal diseases.

From Lab to Life: Multifunctional materials and systems that sense, adapt and perform
Presented by Garrett Melenka, Associate Professor, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Lassonde School of Engineering and Gerd Grau, Associate Professor, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Lassonde School of Engineering
By combining expertise in composite materials and additive manufacturing with printed electronics and sensing systems, Professors Garrett Melenka and Gerd Grau have collaborated on a number of projects from multifunctional carbon fiber composites to wearable smart knee brace technology. These talks bring the two researchers together to discuss how multifunctional materials move from the lab bench to practical, real-world devices.

title: The Sororum Presents: A Step Through Time
location: Bata Shoe Museum, 327 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON, M5S 1W7, Canada
description:
On Saturday, November 14th, join us in the heart of Yorkville as we step into a world of history, art, and craftsmanship. 




Our journey begins at the iconic Bata Shoe Museum, housed within Raymond Moriyama’s award-winning architectural landmark. Here, we’ll uncover fascinating stories of craftsmanship, culture, and human expression before enjoying a hands-on creative experience. 
From the museum, we’ll make our way to the historic Oxley for an intimate lunch and engaging conversation, bringing together the elements that make every Sororum gathering special: discovery, meaningful dialogue, and the joy of connecting with extraordinary women. 
How Our Day Will Unfold
10:30 AM – 12:15 PM | Private Guided Museum Tour 
We’ll begin with a private guided exploration of two remarkable exhibitions, each revealing how something as familiar as footwear can tell extraordinary stories about the people, cultures, and civilizations that came before us. 

Unearthing Vindolanda: Footwear from the Edge of the Roman Empire — Step back nearly 2,000 years and discover remarkably preserved footwear offering a rare and intimate glimpse into everyday life along the northern frontier of the Roman Empire.
Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World — Journey across cultures and generations to discover the beauty, symbolism, and extraordinary artistry of beadwork, and the stories of identity, tradition, and craftsmanship woven into every creation.

12:15 PM – 1:00 PM | A Hands-On Leatherworking Experience 
From appreciating craftsmanship to trying our hand at it! 
We’ll learn about traditional leatherworking techniques before creating our very own custom leather keychain — a beautiful little keepsake to remember the day. 
1:15 PM – 3:00 PM | Lunch & Guided Discussion at The Oxley 
At the heart of every Sororum gathering is the opportunity to connect, share perspectives, and enjoy thoughtful conversation. 
We’ll continue our afternoon at The Oxley, a charming British-inspired restaurant nestled within a late-19th-century Victorian townhouse in Yorkville. With its old-world character and inviting atmosphere, it provides a wonderful setting to gather around the table. 
Over a specially arranged prix fixe lunch, we’ll enjoy delicious food, warm company, and a guided discussion inspired by the stories and discoveries of our morning together. 
3:00 PM Onward | Discover Yorkville 
For those wishing to extend the day, Yorkville awaits! 
Enjoy an afternoon exploring one of Toronto’s most charming neighbourhoods, where historic Victorian streetscapes meet art galleries, inviting cafés, and beautiful boutiques. A lovely opportunity to linger, explore, and enjoy the autumn atmosphere at your own pace. 
Event Details & Pricing
Event Ticket: $75 per person 
Includes: 

Admission to the Bata Shoe Museum
Exclusive private guided museum tour
Hands-on leatherworking workshop and keepsake
Facilitated group discussion at The Oxley

Lunch: $40 per person + applicable taxes 
The Sororum has arranged a special prix fixe menu exclusively for our group. Lunch is paid individually by each guest at the restaurant and is not included in the event ticket. 
More Than an Outing. A Shared Experience.
At The Sororum, we believe the most memorable experiences are those that inspire curiosity, spark meaningful conversation, and bring women together. 
A Step Through Time is an invitation to discover something new, celebrate the artistry and stories of those who came before us, and create a few wonderful memories of our own. 
We look forward to sharing this special day with you.

title: 14th SooRyu Festival - Symbiosis II
