title: Run Your One-Person Business with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
When you're the whole company, the admin never ends: emails, scheduling, proposals, follow-ups. What if you could design a system to handle the busywork?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll learn to design an administrative system for a one-person business with AI as your assistant: intake pipelines, email drafting, client communication, and scheduling. Learn to map work into four piles: what's rules-based, what AI drafts, what needs your judgment, and what should never be automated. You'll build reusable templates and leave with a clearer plan for how AI could help your business.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.

You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.

title: A Short History of Library Architecture in Toronto and Beyond
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, 1st floor
description:
Christopher Hume, the architecture critic and urban issues columnist of the Toronto Star, presents a short history of library architecture. He will be commenting on the structures and social relevance of monumental libraries from Paris, Boston, New York, with a focus on Toronto Public Libraries from around the city.
Hume is the recipient of 2009 The National Newspaper Award for journalism in architecture and urban affairs. His illustrious career at the Toronto Star earned him a President’s Award for Architectural Journalism from the Royal Architectural Institute of Canada. Hume's book, William James’ Toronto Views, won a Toronto Heritage Award in 2000 and in 2004 he received a Landscape Ontario award.

title: Intercultural Communication Competency is a Superpower
description:
This program is part of Fort York Library's
Entrepreneur in Residence
(EIR) service.
How will having “intercultural communication competence” help you in your business? As a newcomer, you have been exposed to different customs, norms, values, and communication styles. Entrepreneur in Residence (Newcomer Focus), Jean Chow, teaches you appropriate and effective words, tones, body gestures and facial expressions when you are negotiating with clients, vendors, partners, employees.
In this session:

description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: The lab of the future: How AI is changing the way we develop new materials
description:
Register now! 
What if AI could help uncover new materials that improve drug delivery, support sustainable agriculture and address environmental challenges? 
By combining artificial intelligence, robotics and automated experimentation, self-driving laboratories are transforming the way new materials and chemical products are discovered. Join Professor Frank Gu (ChemE) as he shares how AI-powered research is accelerating innovation in areas such as drug delivery, agricultural technologies and water treatment, enabling researchers to identify promising solutions faster and more efficiently than ever before. 
Join us on December 2, 2026, at our monthly Skule™ Lunch & Learn. 

By registering for the Skule™ Lunch & Learn event, you could potentially earn Continuing Professional Development (CPD) credits. CPDs are essential for professional engineers and limited license holders to renew their licenses annually through the PEO PEAK Program. If you’re wondering whether this event offering qualifies you for CPD credits, click here to learn more. 

About the speaker
Professor Frank Gu
Professor Frank Gu is the Director of the Institute for Water Innovation, Co-Director, Formulation Self-Driving Lab, Acceleration Consortium and a professor in the Department of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry, where he holds an NSERC Senior Industrial Research Chair in Nanotechnology Engineering. A leading nanotechnology engineer, Dr. Gu has advanced the development of functional nanomaterials with applications in healthcare and environmental sustainability. 
His research spans nanomedicine, drug delivery, AI-powered materials discovery and water treatment. He has helped develop innovative nanomaterials for treating industrial wastewater and advancing drug delivery for eye diseases. In 2015, he founded H2nanO Inc., a company that commercializes energy-efficient water treatment technologies for industrial applications. Throughout his career, Dr. Gu has mentored more than 200 students and research associates, published over 110 peer-reviewed papers, and holds more than 60 issued or pending patents.

title: Tiny Titans: Insects Up Close | Book Launch & Panel Talk with Author & Photographer Dara Ojo
location: North York Central Library, Room 101 - 1st floor
description:
Discover the hidden world of arthropods through stunning macro photography — a visual journey celebrating their beauty, complexity, and essential role in our ecosystems.
Meet
Dara Ojo
, an award-winning macro photographer and conservation storyteller whose work brings the hidden world of arthropods into vivid relief. Ojo's book,
Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem
reveals the fascinating lives of insects, spiders, and other small creatures that quietly sustain life on Earth. Captured across Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, and beyond, Dara Ojo’s photography highlights the intricate details and diversity of these often-overlooked species.
Ojo will be leading the conversation with:
Antonia Guidotti
,
a Collections Technician with a focus on Insects & Arachnids at the Royal Ontario Museum.
Lorraine Johnson
, author and native plant and ecological gardening advocate, bridging the connection between insects, plants, habitat and practical conservation action.
Dr. Sandra Rehan
, professor at York University and principal investigator of the Rehan Lab with a focus on wild bees, pollinator biology and conservation. Rehan's research explores the biology, behaviour and evolution of bees, with a particular interest in understanding and protecting native pollinators.
Dr. Laura Timms
, Senior Specialist of Natural Heritage Management at Credit Valley Conservation and Adjunct Professor with the Daniels Faculty’s Institute of Forestry and Conservation.
Join in this evening to celebrate macro photography and the intricate beauty and ecological importance of insects and spiders, creatures that quietly anchor global biodiversity, pollination, and climate resilience.
Free program. Register for a reminder.
***Doors open at 5:30 pm. At 6:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached.***
5:30 pm:
Doors open. Mingle and chat with fellow nature and environmental enthusiasts!
6:00 pm:
Presentation begins. Enjoy a highly visual presentation combining photography, science, conservation and storytelling, taking the audience behind the scenes of six years documenting tiny worlds across five continents and exploring why these overlooked species matter. A light, informal conversation with guest speakers will explore why arthropods are so essential to our ecosystems, with a discussion of challenges impacting local species, and how science, photography and art can work together to help people notice, understand and care about the natural world. An audience Q&A follows this discussion.
7:30 pm:
Book signing with books available for purchase.
***
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​
Questions? Please contact North York Central Library - Business, Science & Technology Department.
***
Place a hold or borrow from Toronto Public Library:
Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem
(book) - Dara Ojo
A Garden for the Rusty-patched Bumblebee
(book) - Lorraine Johnson

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

description:

The Dining Room : Exploring the Design of Twelve Iconic Rooms in Search of the Perfect Dining Experience.​
​(Random House, 2026).
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an englightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dning. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherised moments we share within them will delight armchair travellers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.

title: Colloquium (Olivia Bailey, UC Berkeley)
description:
The Department is pleased to welcome Olivia Bailey, an assistant professor in the Department of Philosophy, at UC Berkeley for a colloquium on December 3, 2026. She works on questions in moral psychology and the history of moral philosophy (particularly the British moralists). Her current research is concerned with the ethical and epistemic significance of empathy. 
Title
The See-Through Heart: Transparency, Rationality, and Emotional Self-Knowledge 
Abstract
How can I arrive at an answer to the question of how I feel? I could study my behavior, or defer to my psychoanalyst. But it is hard to resist the idea that there is another way that I—and I alone—can speak to the question of what I feel, one that does not rely on such indirect observational routes. One potentially powerful lead, here, is the fact that I can ordinarily expect my thinking about my feelings to make a difference to what I feel. Perhaps it is no coincidence that I have both a special way to answer the question of how I feel and a special power to shape my feelings through thought. 
I consider two established ways of developing this lead, an interpretationist view and a transparency view, and draw out problems for both I then look to the phenomenology of emotional experience for help developing a hybrid of the two that avoids both sets of problems. On this account, my (and yet special) ordinary authority to say what my emotion is hinges on my power to ‘make up my heart’ by settling a question about the relationship between my inner state and the world.

In this session, we’ll exercise our Compromise muscles. In a democracy, we find solutions together. When we make room for each other's approaches, more people can accept the decisions. Through a 30-min series of short, interactive exercises, you'll find out how you prefer to make decisions, practice solving a problem with those who think like you, and practice compromising with those who might think differently. This workshop will strengthen your ability to engage in meaningful dialogue.

description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.

Ticket link: http://bit.ly/SilkwormWL


On sale now!


Storied and influential American indie-rock band Silkworm comes back to Toronto for the first time in 26 years!


Formed in 1987, Silkworm is revered by those in the know. Relocating from Missoula, Montana to Seattle and eventually Chicago, the band has released nine acclaimed albums on iconic labels including Matador and Touch and Go Records. They disbanded in 2005 following drummer Michael Dahlquist tragic passing, and reunited in 2024 to honour their late friend and collaborator Steve Albini, joined by drummer Jeff Panall (Songs: Ohia, Mint Mile). Playing together as a quartet for the first time in 30 years proved both emotional and exhilarating, inspiring a long-awaited return to the stage.

The band's enduring legacy is celebrated in the documentary Couldn't You Wait: The Story of Silkworm and the forthcoming book Lay It Down in Full View.

For their historic return to Toronto, Silkworm will be joined by Fines, the songwriting project of Darcy Hancock. Many listeners will remember Hancock as a member of Vancouver’s indie-rock favourites, Ladyhawk, whose records and non-stop touring helped establish them as one of Canada's most beloved guitar bands of the 2000s.

Poster by Julia Araïche

location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Computers for Beginners
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Past & Present: Lost in Translation
description:
Past & Present: Lost in Translation

Past & Present: Lost in Translation Friday, December 04, 1:00 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. Virtual Panel via YouTube Join Onsite Gallery for a thought-provoking virtual panel featuring Alize Zorlutuna, Richa Narvekar, Dedra McDermottand others exploring how artists draw on cultural traditions, ancestral knowledge, and diasporic ways of knowing to shape contemporary creative practices. The discussion will focus on how visual art, dance, design, storytelling, and material practices can reinterpret cultural knowledge while creating new relationships to memory, identity, land, material culture, and the more-than-human. The panelists will share how their practices engage with inherited traditions, not simply as forms to preserve, but as living sources for experimentation, reclamation, and new ways of understanding the present. Stay involved with a live Q&A session, moderated by Onsite Gallery’s Programs & Community Coordinator, Susan Jama . ASL Interpretation will be available. The panel is live-streamed via YouTube Visit Registration Page About the Panelists Images (left to right): Alize Zorlutuna photo by Farihah Aliyah Shaw. Richa Narvekar Alize Zorlutuna is a queer interdisciplinary artist, writer, and educator whose practice explores relationships between land, material culture, and the more-than-human through diasporic ways of knowing. Moving between Tkarónto and Anatolia has cultivated an attentiveness to sites of encounter, where bodies, geographies, and elemental forces meet in ongoing processes of negotiation and co-becoming. Drawing on material and relational traditions from the SWANA region, their work spans video, installation, ebru (Anatolian water marbling), ceramics, textiles, and participatory practice, bringing together diverse materials, methods, and geographies to consider place, memory, and relation. Richa Narvekar is an Architectural Designer and Visual Artist that is interested in the connect between Art, Architecture, Urban and Interior Design. She earned her Bachelors in Architecture at CEPT University, India and was a British Council scholar to the Masters in Architecture, Urban Design program at The Bartlett School of Architecture, London, UK. She is a registered Architect under the Council of Architecture, India and holds 15+ years of experience across India and Canada. Her practice, based out of Toronto, Canada and Goa, India is multidisciplinary, with a focus on projects in Interior Design. She has led several interior design and build projects as a Senior Designer for firms in the Greater Toronto Area. She is also involved with sustainable architectural projects and community focused art and urban initiatives in both Canada and India. Her work is centered on an exploration of vernacular, critical regionalist, decolonial and anti-capitalist approaches to material and ways of making. Images (left to right): Dedra McDermott photo by Christine Do. Susan Jama . Dedra McDermott is a Black artist-researcher, curator, producer, movement dramaturg, and cultural steward working at the intersection of choreographic performance, archival practice, and visual culture. Following a successful career as a professional contemporary dancer across stage and screen, two significant concussions in 2018 catalyzed a profound pivot toward creative leadership. Since then, Dedra has charted a rapid, wide-ranging trajectory, navigating a nimble transition from emerging to mid-career practice. Grounded by a multifaceted academic foundation (BFA ’16, MA ’20, MFA ’24), her cross-disciplinary work champions racialized artists navigating complex creative processes. As an evolving arts leader, she supports creators re-educating the public on global Indigeneity and Black diasporic histories across Latin America and the Caribbean. Dedra is one of the former Co-Executive Artistic Producers of DanceWorks (2023–25). During her tenure, she curated and produced over 15 live presentations and choreographic development programs, while leading access-based initiatives for hard-of-hearing and d/Deaf audiences alongside community partners like VibraFusionLab. As a cultural steward who values the art of gathering, Dedra works equitably to bring a diverse public together—creating the conditions for deeper cultural connection and appreciation. About the Moderator Susan Jama is an art worker with over 6 years of experience leading community engagement and public arts programming with strong grassroots experience. She is the Programs and Community Coordinator at Onsite Gallery. Susan has worked with various institutions that approach heritage in a community-minded manner including Toronto Ward Museum (TWM) and Black Artists’ Networks in Dialogue Gallery & Cultural Centre (BAND). She graduated with a Masters of Museum Studies from University of Toronto and completed her Bachelor in Psychology & History at York University. She currently serves on the Museum Education Roundtable board as co-treasurer.

title: Art of Darkness: Edgar Allan Poe's Life & Work
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Professor Emily Ogden shares her intimate inquiry into the shadowy life and compelling work of the definitive author of the macabre.
Since Edgar Allan Poe’s mysterious death in 1849, his stories and poems have captivated millions of readers around the world. Nearly two centuries later, why do we continue to descend into the darkness of his imagination—and of the genres, from horror to crime, that he pioneered?
In Darkness Becomes Bright, Ogden plumbs the darkness within Poe and enters it alongside him. She interweaves stories from his mysterious and tragic life with those of his most famous readers and translators, showing us how Poe’s vision echoes across the generations, allowing us to make peace with our own flawed humanity.
Emily Ogden speaks with author and critic Naben Ruthnum about the brief life and immortal art of Edgar Allan Poe.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Emily Ogden
Naben Ruthnum

title: Vietnam & Cambodia with Angkor Wat! Ancient Kingdoms of Southeast Asia!!
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
A Meetup trip in December . . . what can be a better gift for the holidays?! Join our travelers group on a captivating 14-day journey through the heart of Southeast Asia as we explore the vibrant cultures and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam & Cambodia (Dec 04-18, 2026)

As with all our tailor-made Meetup trips, our expert guides will lead us off the beaten path to uncover the authentic charm of each destination, while comfortable accommodations and delicious local cuisine ensure a truly immersive travel experience. Embark on an unforgettable journey through the vibrant cities and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam, finishing with the wonders of Cambodia.

We begin in Hanoi, where history and culture come alive, then sail the emerald waters of Halong Bay. Step back in time among the imperial treasures of Hue, wander the lantern-lit streets of charming Hoi An, and feel the dynamic energy of Ho Chi Minh City. We conclude your adventure at the awe-inspiring temples of Siem Reap, home to the legendary Angkor Wat.

TRIP HIGHLIGHTS:

* **Hanoi**; explore Ho Chi Minh sites, Temple of Literature, Old Quarter cyclo ride & water puppet show
* Visit rural **craft villages**: conical hat & incense making, home-hosted lunch, village walk
* **Ha Long Bay cruise**: limestone islands, floating villages, cave visit, Tai Chi & sunset views
* **Hue**: Perfume River boat ride, Thien Mu Pagoda, Khai Dinh’s Tomb & Imperial Citadel
* Scenic **Hai Van Pass train** to Danang; explore Dragon Bridge, Cham Museum, Marble Mountain
* **Hoi An Ancient Town** (UNESCO), visit tailor shops, pottery village & organic farm with cooking class
* **Ho Chi Minh City & Cu Chi Tunnels**; War Remnants Museum, Reunification Palace & Ben Thanh Market
* **Mekong Delta cruise**: coconut workshops, sampan ride, orchards & lunch in riverside village
* **Siem Reap**: dinner with Apsara dance, Angkor temples (Ta Prohm, Bayon, Angkor Wat)
* Cambodian cultural immersion: **monk blessing**, village crafts & cooking, **Tonle Sap Lake sunset cruise**

location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Silent Lake Loop
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**This adventure is sold out. Please [join the waitlist on our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/silent-lake-loop)**
**This adventure is exclusive to Explorer members.**
**We’ve wanted to hike this trail for years. There’s 15km of undeveloped shoreline with very few people around a beautiful looped trail. We finally have the opportunity to tackle it in this Explorer exclusive.**
The Shoreline Trail starts from the day use lot on a flat, easy path that eases the group in. From there it settles beside the water and stays close to it for the rest of the hike, with the lake appearing and disappearing through the trees.
The scenery shifts every few kilometres as the trail moves between low, shaded ground and higher, drier forest. Viewpoints along the way give us places to stop and look out over the water, and we’ll take a long lunch at one of them.
It’s a small group and a long trail, which means plenty of time to talk. By the time we reach lunch at the lookout, the conversation will have covered about as much ground as the trail.
Check the trip plan (available on the website after registration) for the details, including the meeting point, gear list, and timing for the day.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Silent Lake Lookouts:** Most of the park’s lookout points are along this trail, with wide views across the water.
**Isolated Landscape:** A day with a trail entirely to yourself.
**Beaver Meadows:** The trail crosses open meadow flats where beavers have reshaped the landscape. It’s a good stretch for spotting birds and watching the light change
**Itinerary**
**06:30** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**10:00 - 16:00** \- Hike Shoreline trail
**16:00** \- Anticipated return to cars
**19:30** \- Anticipated return to Toronto
**Event cost: $65+HST. $60 optional transport also available. Join the waitlist [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/silent-lake-loop)**

title: Design Your Own Mahjong Tiles Workshop
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Design Your Own Mahjong Tiles Workshop            
                                
    



    
         
    




	

	


			
Events
	







	

	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Saturday December 5, 2026
10:00 am – 12:00 pm 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    In this hands-on workshop, participants will design and glaze a set of 4 ceramic Mahjong tiles using underglaze techniques. Guided by artist Joshua Lue Chee Kong, explore pattern-making, symbolism, and personal storytelling through clay. No experience needed. Just bring your stories, creativity, and inspiration! 
Then, join us on Wednesday December 16 from 6:00 – 8:00 pm for a Mahjong Social Night, where you can view the complete set of community-designed tiles, play a game of Mahjong, and take home your tiles. The tiles will be documented as part of the Mahjong Stories Archive, a collective archive of personal stories connected to Mahjong. 

                
                    
    

	




			

    
        
             
                
                    Your ticket includes one workshop and access to the Mahjong Social Night. 

                
                    
    



        
          
          
                        
               
                Gardiner Friends : $30
                                        
                        
               
                General : $35
                                        
                      

           
            
              Gardiner Friends, log in to access your discount.* 
Not a Gardiner Friend yet? Join now at the Friend level or above to save . 
*Discounts on programs and classes do not apply to ‘Annual Pass’ level. 
            
                    
          
            
  
            
                
                                    SOLD OUT
                
                            
           
                
                
                    
                        
                    
                
                
          
          
        

	







    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    Important Information: 

                
                    
    



    
        
             
                
                    
Please ensure the course you choose works with your schedule. This class is non-refundable and non-transferrable, regardless of the reason for withdrawal.
By signing up for this class, participants are committing to abide by the Museum’s Code of Conduct, Ticketing Policy, and Studio Policy.

Gardiner Friends, please log in to access your discount. Gardiner Friends may only purchase adult clay classes at the discounted rate for membership card holders. 

                
                    
    



    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    Instructor
                    
                
                
                    Joshua Lue Chee Kong
                    
                
                
                    Joshua Lue Chee Kong is a multidisciplinary artist from Trinidad and Tobago based in Toronto. Working across ceramics, sculpture, digital media, and community-focused projects, he explores how objects carry personal history and cultural identities across geographical boundaries. His practice draws on nostalgia and transforms familiar forms into opportunities for storytelling, connection, and belonging. 
In 2026, Joshua co-founded DeNarrative Studio with Barry Ling to support people in telling their stories through art. Their Designing Your Own Mahjong Tiles workshop grew out of their own life experiences and familial memories surrounding mahjong tiles, using the tiles’ long history and physical form as a platform for others to express their stories.

title: GenTO: Toronto AI Film Festival
location: Innis Town Hall,2 Sussex Ave, Toronto, ON M5S 1J5, Canada
description:
GenTO: Toronto AI Film Festival is a celebration of the emerging world of AI-enhanced filmmaking, bringing together filmmakers, artists, creative technologists and film enthusiasts to explore the evolving possibilities of cinematic storytelling.

Taking place on December 5, 2026, at Innis Town Hall, University of Toronto, the festival showcases a curated selection of AI-assisted short films, advertisements and music videos from creators around the world, alongside filmmaker Q&As, industry panels, behind-the-scenes discussions, networking opportunities and an awards ceremony recognizing creative excellence.

As AI filmmaking gains momentum in Toronto and across Canada, GenTO provides a platform for the growing community of creators to showcase their work, exchange ideas and connect with industry professionals. By bringing international perspectives to Toronto's vibrant film culture, the festival aims to foster dialogue, experimentation and collaboration at the intersection of filmmaking and emerging technology.

The festival offers filmmakers and creative professionals opportunities to discover emerging storytelling techniques, engage with industry peers and build meaningful connections, while inviting film enthusiasts to experience new forms of cinematic expression and explore the future of filmmaking.

More Info: gento.ca/festival https://gento.ca/festival

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join us and learn about the world and keep active and warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life.

Jane Franklin was a prominent 19th-century British woman known for her remarkable energy, and influence, in exploration and colonial affairs during the Victorian era.

She is best remembered as the wife of John Franklin, the Royal Navy officer who led the ill-fated Franklin Expedition. After her husband disappeared in the Arctic in 1847, Jane Franklin became one of the most determined figures in the search for him. She funded expeditions, and lobbied the British government. She mobilized public attention for decades in an effort to uncover his fate and learn the truth.

But she wasn’t only defined by that search. Jane Franklin was also a widely travelled and intellectually curious woman who visited places like Tasmania (then Van Diemen’s Land), Greece, the Middle East, and Russia.

She also supported education, and science, often working behind the scenes to influence institutions like the Royal Geographical Society. You could say she became a kind of unofficial power broker in British exploration.

In this lecture, we’ll explore the life and times of Jane Franklin. in the new biography series of timely women and men who made the world.

description:
Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use?
A panel of experts, alongside our Innovator-in-Residence
Ryan Kelln
, who know AI from very different angles, unite for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about:
The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them.
Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here.
Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours).

Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.

title: Landmarks 6: Gladstone Hotel to The Edgewater Hotel Via Gutta Percha
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**

Toronto is a city that hides its history in plain sight. Beneath the glass towers are layers of stories — grand hotels that vanished overnight, political scandals whispered through stone corridors, theatres that once glittered under gaslight, and laneways where the city first learned how to become a metropolis.

This new Toronto History Walks tour invites the walker to slow down, and see the city differently.

Let's return to a bygone era: late 1930s. Parkdale would already have had a long fascinating history behind it, but you would also be looking at a neighbourhood that was changing with the times. One of the most interesting examples was the Edgewater Hotel, built in 1939 at 14 Roncesvalles Avenue, at The Queensway.

It was built by Fred Hammer and became part of a very busy transportation hub, sitting beside the Sunnyside Bus Terminal. The building has survived, although the Edgewater name eventually disappeared and the hotel went through several incarnations. It is a wonderful reminder that Parkdale's history isn't just Victorian, there is twentieth-century history here as well.

And then we come to the Gladstone Hotel, which is one of those buildings that almost seem to have been watching the neighbourhood change. The hotel we see today dates from 1889 and was designed by Toronto architect George Martell Miller in the Richardsonian Romanesque style. Its location was absolutely perfect for business: it stood across from the Parkdale railway station, and was close to the Exhibition grounds. Travelling salesmen, railway workers, visitors to the CNE and commercial travellers could all find shelter here.

The original owner was Susanna Robinson, who was left a widow with thirteen children before construction of the hotel was completed.
The Gladstone tells us something important about Parkdale itself. For decades it was a working-class gathering place, and as the factories and industries changed, so did the fortunes of the hotel. The great tower once had a cupola that could be seen from a distance, but that disappeared in the 1940s. By the later twentieth century the hotel had fallen on hard times and had developed a much different reputation. Yet it never completely lost its role as a community gathering place.

Eventually it was restored and reinvented, becoming part of the artistic and cultural life of Queen Street West.

And finally, we get to one of the great industrial stories of old Parkdale — the Gutta Percha & Rubber Manufacturing Company. Established here in 1883 on West Lodge Avenue, the factory became one of the largest employers in the neighbourhood and, at its height, the largest rubber manufacturer in Canada. They made all sorts of rubber products — hose, belting, boots, footwear, mats and eventually products connected with the rapidly growing automobile industry.

The factory operated until 1960, when changing technology, synthetic rubber and competition finally brought its long Parkdale story to an end. Three places — the Edgewater, the Gladstone and Gutta Percha — give us three very different Parkdales: the Parkdale of travel and transportation, the Parkdale of hotels and community life, and the Parkdale of factories and working people. Put them together and you begin to see just how fascinating this neighbourhood really is.

This walking tour begins at The Gladstone Hotel at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Gladstone Avenue, one block east of Dufferin Street. We end at the corner of Queen Street West and Roncesvalles Avenue.

This walking tour is for all walking levels. Please dress for the season, and hope to see you there.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Niagara Falls on Foot
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/niagara-falls)**
**Most people who come to Niagara Falls stop at the railing. We’re going beyond the falls, to the part most visitors never see.**
We’ll start where everyone starts, on the path beside the falls. It’s busy, so we’ll take our time, find a good spot, and get the photos done before the crowds thicken.
Then we leave the crowds behind. A short drive away is the Niagara Glen Nature Reserve, a protected pocket of forest deep inside the gorge. We’ll take the stairways down to the river and hike a 6km loop along the Niagara River that ends at the Whirlpool. On the way we’ll wind through huge boulders scattered across the gorge floor, stopping for lunch on one of the flat spots in the reserve and moving at a pace that works for the group.
See the falls from above, then walk the river below as the gorge walls rise on either side. Both ends of the same river, in one day.
Check the trip plan for the details, including the meeting point, gear list, and timing for the day.
**Because this adventure includes multiple stops, taking our shared transport is mandatory. Transport is included in the cost of this adventure.**
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Niagara Falls:** The full weight of the Niagara River dropping over the edge, with the roar and spray carrying along the gorge rim.
**Boulder Fields:** Large boulders left behind as the Niagara River eroded through the gorge, now draped in mosses and ferns.
**The Niagara Whirlpool:** The river hits a bend in the gorge and has nowhere to go but around, spinning into a slow, churning circle.
**Itinerary**
**08:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**10:00 - 11:45** \- Walk the Niagara Falls path
**11:45 - 12:00** \- Drive to Niagara Glen
**12:00 - 15:30** \- Hike Niagara Glen and Whirlpool trails\, with a stop for lunch
**15:30 - 18:00** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $120+HST. Transportation is included in the cost of the adventure. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/niagara-falls)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

description:
Design Your Own Mahjong Tiles Workshop            
                                
    



    
         
    




	

	


			
Events
	







	

	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Sunday December 6, 2026
10:00 am – 12:00 pm 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    In this hands-on workshop, participants will design and glaze a set of 4 ceramic Mahjong tiles using underglaze techniques. Guided by artist Joshua Lue Chee Kong, explore pattern-making, symbolism, and personal storytelling through clay. No experience needed. Just bring your stories, creativity, and inspiration! 
Then, join us on Wednesday December 16 from 6:00 – 8:00 pm for a Mahjong Social Night, where you can view the complete set of community-designed tiles, play a game of Mahjong, and take home your tiles. The tiles will be documented as part of the Mahjong Stories Archive, a collective archive of personal stories connected to Mahjong.

Gardiner Friends, please log in to access your discount. Gardiner Friends may only purchase adult clay classes at the discounted rate for membership card holders. 

                
                    
    



    
        
                            
                    
                        
                    
                
                       
            
                
                    Instructor
                    
                
                
                    Joshua Lue Chee Kong
                    
                
                
                    Joshua Lue Chee Kong is a multidisciplinary artist from Trinidad and Tobago based in Toronto. Working across ceramics, sculpture, digital media, and community-focused projects, he explores how objects carry personal history and cultural identities across geographical boundaries. His practice draws on nostalgia and transforms familiar forms into opportunities for storytelling, connection, and belonging. 
In 2026, Joshua co-founded DeNarrative Studio with Barry Ling to support people in telling their stories through art. Their Designing Your Own Mahjong Tiles workshop grew out of their own life experiences and familial memories surrounding mahjong tiles, using the tiles’ long history and physical form as a platform for others to express their stories.

Hiking with Mo is always a treat! You will be guaranteed a history lesson or a bad joke!
This hike hits the sweet spot for intermediate hikers, blending the rugged terrain of the **Niagara Escarpment** with dramatic cliffside views without requiring an exhausting all-day commitment.
Hike Overview
Begin your trek on a wide, forested path that gradually transitions into the the escarpment terrain —packed with exposed cedar roots, limestone steps, and uneven rock formations that will keep your feet engaged.
The highlight of the route is the stretch along the cliff edges, From this vantage point, you will stand high above the Lowville Valley, looking down on the canopy and watching turkey vultures ride the thermal updrafts right at eye level. Keep an eye out for the ancient, twisted cliff-edge cedars, some of which have survived here for over 800 years.
This is a great hike at this time of year!
Please ensure you have proper footwear, lots of water and snacks!
source: Meetup: These Boots Are Made for Hiking

title: Christmas in Old Toronto! 1855 - The Railway Era (NEW FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**So what was it like in Toronto in 1855 at Christmas time? This tour is different from the first part - Christmas in 1833 York. If you can, try and take both tours, and compare the differences in 22 years of history! Toronto changed significantly between those years.**

Imagine spending Christmas in Toronto in 1855, when the city was still a relatively young place and the streets were a far cry from the Toronto we know today. There would be no electric Christmas lights, no department-store displays, no traffic jams of cars on the DVP. Instead, Toronto was a city of horse-drawn wagons, muddy streets, wood fires, gas lamps, small shops and busy markets. And the railways were on the way to Toronto.

Christmas was becoming increasingly popular as a family celebration, influenced by traditions coming from Britain, Ireland, Europe and the United States. For many, Christmas Day meant attending church, visiting relatives and friends, enjoying a special meal and taking a welcome break from everyday life, even if just for a day.

For children, Christmas could be magical, but it was a much simpler Christmas. Toys were homemade or relatively inexpensive, and a child's Christmas might include a wooden toy, a doll, some sweets, an orange, nuts or perhaps a book. There were no shopping malls or endless advertisements telling people what they needed to buy.

Toronto's shops and markets would nevertheless have been busy in the days before Christmas. The smell of roasting meat, baked goods, spices and coal fires would have filled the air, while church bells and carriages would have been part of the Christmas landscape. And for those who were poor, Christmas could be a very different experience, making charitable giving and church relief particularly important.

But perhaps the most fascinating thing about Christmas in 1855 is how close the holiday still was to the realities of nineteenth-century life. Toronto was a city of immigrants, workers, merchants, labourers, professionals and families living in very different circumstances. Some homes would have been warm and comfortable, while others would have been cold, and crowded. There were no modern hospitals, no antibiotics, no central heating and no easy way of escaping a harsh winter. Yet people celebrated, rich or poor.

They gathered around fireplaces, went to church, shared food, told stories and tried to make Christmas special. So when we walk through Toronto and imagine Christmas in 1855, we're not simply looking at an old-fashioned Christmas, we're stepping into a city where Christmas was beginning to take on many of the traditions we recognize today, but where life itself was more uncertain.

This tour explores old Toronto during the Christmas season of 1855. This walking tour is for all walking levels. The tour begins and ends at St. James Cathedral on King Street East at Church Street. A great way to kick off the season.

This tour has a ticketed price of $15.00.

**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Forest Bathing at the Garden
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Connect with nature and join us for a guided forest therapy walk!
Discover the beauty of nature in winter through a guided outdoor forest bathing walk with certified forest therapy guide Laura Bincik. At a slow pace and in community with other participants and the environment, you will be guided by a series of invitations throughout the experience to awaken your senses and intentionally connect with nature in the present moment.
 
We will gather briefly indoors to prepare for the walk and consider the origin of forest bathing as well as some of the benefits of the practice. When we venture into the Toronto Botanical Gardens and cover approximately 1.5 km on paved pathways, lawns and bare ground, at times encountering uneven terrain, inclines and declines. We will be strolling, standing and sitting (if you wish to). Your comfort and safety are most important!
 
Please note: The surrounding Wilket Creek Ravine faced severe damage due to flooding and has unfortunately remained closed to the public until repairs can be made. The upcoming Forest Bathing Walk will not cross any closed trails into the ravine.
 
As this program occurs outdoors, please dress for the weather by wearing sturdy, insulated footwear, an insulated jacket, a hat, scarf and mittens. You may wish to bring a water bottle, sunglasses, walking poles and/or a folding stool for your comfort.
 
As the walk ends, we will gather and partake in a seasonal tea and snacks, and taste honey harvested at Toronto Botanical Garden.
 
In the event of severe weather or environmental conditions, TBG staff will make alternative arrangements to the program.
 
Washrooms are available onsite.
 
The program is suited for adults 18+. All participants must sign a liability waiver at the start of the program.
 
Sunday, December 6, 1 to 3 p.m.
Registration: Public $35, TBG Members $30 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Laura Bincik
Laura Bincik is a certified forest therapy guide with the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Following a career that straddled health care and education, Laura discovered that her lifelong sense of awe for the natural world could be enriched and shared with others to enhance wellbeing. Laura feels a connection to the land and the wonder of being in nature from countless hours spent exploring Toronto ravines in all seasons. An active member of Nature and Forest Therapy Canada, Laura follows the growing research on the mental and physical health benefits of forest bathing and is expanding her practice by connecting with local, national, and international leaders in the field.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends: Author Talk with A.D. Sui
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall (first floor)
description:
In this exciting author talk A.D. Sui will discuss their upcoming novel Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends, a sapphic cli-fi thriller, as well as science fiction's role in today's rapidly politically and technologically changing world. Question and answer period to follow.
This sapphic cli-fi thriller is a love letter to hope in the bleakest of times, combining the multiverse-bending drama of This Is How You Lose the Time War with the cat-and-mouse chase of Killing Eve.
On a near-future Earth devastated by climate change, Dr. Cassandra Barlowe is right where she wants to be: working on an island of floating trash in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, as far away from Dr. Yana Gulsvig as possible. Cas’s research on plastic-dissolving fungi is undervalued and underfunded, thanks to the invention of deleria, a drug that allows glimpses into different timelines. For the average user, it’s a way to view lost loved ones or experience a different life, but it also offers a glimpse into worlds where humanity has solved its many global crises. Now, most science funding is dedicated to trawling these different timelines, searching for a reality with the solution to the climate devastation.
But when Yana — the world’s leading expert on deleria and Cassandra’s ex-lover — is killed in a mysterious explosion in the hub of deleria research, taking the hope of reversing climate change with her, Cas is arrested on charges of domestic terrorism. Cas must delve through timelines to piece together what happened, while watching other versions of herself and Yana live out the life they could have had — happier, more in love. As brutal government agents close in and her addiction to deleria grows, Cas has to make a choice: live in the spiraling branches of reality, seeking closure for Yana’s death until the drug shatters her mind, or live in the now, even if that means embracing her own damaged self and fighting, however hopelessly, for her own future and that of humanity.

title: Birds and Our Christmas Traditions
description:
Birds are woven into the fabric of Christmas traditions, serving as powerful symbols of hope, renewal, and warmth during the winter months. Their presence during the holidays, whether through festive ornaments, songs, or sightings at feeders, recalls ancient lore that connects birds with messages of love and positivity. By inviting birds into our lives and honoring them through tradition, we not only support these treasured visitors but also embrace the spirit of Christmas—one of generosity, harmony, and the celebration of nature’s enduring beauty. Jim Mackiewicz is the owner of Wild Birds Unlimited and has been helping customers with backyard bird feeding and connecting to nature for 25 years.

title: Python Essentials 1 and 2 Learning Circle
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Tuesday afternoons from September 22 to December 8, 2-3:30pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Learners who successfully complete both courses will earn a digital badge and certificate of completion.
Python Essentials 1
is the first in a 2-course series that teaches computer programming skills including how to design, develop, and improve computer programs using the Python programming language. The course covers essential programming topics such as data types, variables, control flow, functions, and exceptions.
Python Essentials 2
is the second in a 2-course series that will prepare you for the PCAP – Certified Associate in Python Programming certification exam at Pearson VUE. This intermediate-level course covers advanced aspects of Python programming, including modules, packages, exceptions, file processing and object-oriented programming (OOP).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: Free/PWYC Double Feature You've Got Mail + Winter Village (Distillery District)
description:
Experience Toronto
**Note: I recommend obtaining your ticket as soon as possible, as there are a limited number of seats**

**On Tuesday, December 8th, see** **Soulpepper's Double Feature** **You've Got Mail and Shop Around the Corner, plus get free, skip-the-line entry into the famous Winter Village at The Distillery District**. Be part of **Soulpepper's** **first dedicated Civic Programming lineup** rooted in a simple belief: arts spaces should also be public spaces, where people can experience culture, exchange ideas and connect, with or without a ticket. All seats are general addminssion. **Purchase your Free/PWYC ticket for You've Got Mail and Shop Around the Corner on Tuesday, December 8th at 7pm.**

**Shop Around the Corner (1940):** Two employees at a gift shop can barely stand one another, without realizing that they are falling in love through the post as each other’s anonymous pen pal.

**You’ve Got Mail (1998):** A boutique bookshop owner and a corporate chain store owner who despise each other in real life unwittingly fall in love over the Internet.

**Costa Rica’s Río Celeste Chocolate Waterfall**
Snack on chocolate-drizzled pineapple and banana treats, then step through an augmented reality portal to explore Costa Rica’s natural beauty.

**Santa’s Village at Soulpepper**
Inspired by Soulpepper Theatre’s production of “Parfumerie,” this whimsical Christmas world takes over the theatre atrium. Step into Santa’s Village with twinkling lights, displays, a vintage-inspired letter-writing station, specialty hot chocolates and, of course, Santa and his elves.

**Festive food and drinks**
With more than 50 vendors and outdoor bars, the Distillery Winter Village is a true foodie destination. New this year: Prince St. Pizza, Carousel Bakery, Sweet Crumble, Potato Bar and Peacock Bakehouse. Chef’s Lane returns following a strong debut last year, with four acclaimed chefs: Michael Angeloni, Afrim Pristine, Taylor Wells and Arush Vardhan Singh.

**Naughty or Nice Bar at Pure Spirits Courtyard** — one of the village’s signature outdoor bars — now updated with 50,000 white-and-blue holiday lights and a long communal table.

**COST**
Regular: Pay What You Can $0/ 15/ 20
Seats are general admission.

Meetup Organizer Fee: $5

Ticket Policy: All sales are final.

**SIGNING-UP**

* **RSVP, confirming if you will join for Winter Village only, or Winter Village and the Movies**
* **[Purchase](https://my.soulpepper.ca/16473/16483) your Free/ PWYC ticket for Tuesday December 8th at 7pm, and post you have your ticket in the Comment section. I will then move you to attending.**
* Members can also show up at the Theatre at event start time with their ticket in hand.

RSVPs close 2 days prior, hoping there will still be tickets. Cancellations may result in a No Show and impact future attendance.

A reminder will be sent the day before with my cell and reminder details where to meet and when.

**MEETUP TIME**
**Meet me for the Winter Village at: 5:45pm in front of Young Centre for the Performing Arts in the Distillery District at 50 Tankhouse Lane.**
We will wait 5 mins.

**Meet me for the show at: 6:30pm in the line for the Garland Cabaret inside the Young Centre for the Performing Arts in the Distillery District at 50 Tankhouse Lane**

Once we have grabbed our seats, we can take turns buying food inside the Theatre - sandwiches, salads, pastries, beverages..

**Show Starts**: **7pm**

You've Got Mail Length: 2 hours
Shop around the Corner Length: 1 hour 37 mins

**After: meet at the same spot to chat about the show before heading home**

Enjoy and please post your comments in the Event after!

title: Classical & Latin American Guitar Performance
description:
Karla García is a Chilean-Canadian guitarist, music creator, and educator based in Toronto. Originally from Chiloé, Chile, she has performed as a soloist and collaborator with orchestras and ensembles in Canada and Latin America. Her musical work brings together classical guitar, Latin American music, popular music, and original songs. Karla studied guitar at the University of Chile and has performed with orchestras including the Ontario Pops Orchestra and the Scarborough Philharmonic Orchestra. As an educator, she is passionate about creating welcoming and engaging learning experiences that help students develop confidence and a lasting connection with music.

description: Held, by 2024 Scotiabank Giller Prize winner Anne Michaels, is a luminous, fragmented novel about love, memory, and the reverberations of war across generations. Beginning on a First World War battlefield, the narrative moves through time and place to explore how desire and grief endure beyond a single lifetime. Michaels – renowned poet and author of Fugitive Pieces—weaves history and intimacy into a work of haunting beauty. By the Lake Book Club hosts six Tuesday-night events from February to December with top Canadian authors and Humber Polytechnics alumni. Each in-person event features readings, discussions, Q&A, book signings and ASL interpretation, while virtual sessions include live subtitles and audio access.

title: Instructional Skills Workshop (ISW) (IN-PERSON) – December 9, 10, 11, 2026
description:
This 3-day intensive workshop encourages examination of one’s teaching practices with feedback focused on the learning process rather than on the specific lesson content. The ISW engenders participatory learning and community building that can transfer back into the classroom. Participants work collaboratively in a small group setting of 4-5 participants to further develop their teaching effectiveness as they design and lead three 10-minute lessons. Following each, participants receive reflective verbal, written, and video feedback from the other participants who have been learners.
This certificate is open to all faculty members (research stream, teaching stream, contract).
This certificate is also available for graduate students with at least 3 years of teaching experience. Alternatively, graduate students are invited to complete the Teaching Assistant Certificate in Teaching (TACT) ( https://www.yorku.ca/teachingcommons/certificates/#tact ).
This is a three-day workshop series scheduled for Wednesday December 9, Thursday December 10, and Friday December 11. Each day will run from 9 am to 4:30 pm in DB 1014.
** Please kindly note: this is a 3-day workshop series intended for participants to attend  the entire workshop (all three days from 9am-4:30pm) in-person.
Register using our registration form ( https://teachingcommonsforms.apps01.yorku.ca/forms/view.php?id=1163054 ).

title: Photo Editing with Photoshop
description:
Adobe Photoshop is the world’s best imaging and graphic design software and is at the core of just about every creative project, from photo editing and compositing to digital painting, animation, and graphic design.
Join us for an introductory lesson and learn about the most common tools. We'll explore the workspace and enhance images while investigating tools such as crop, levels, colour balance and more. See how an image can be altered and repaired using patch tools such as the clone and healing brush tools. We'll also dive deep into the world of layers and how you can manage them for those really unique and fun projects.
Registration is required.

title: Building Your Website with WordPress Session 3
description:

integrate lead generation tools with participants' email systems, ensuring visitors can easily find
information and connect with the business across all devices.
KEYWORDS: NAVIGATION MENUS · ELEMENTOR PAGE BUILDER · SUB-PAGES · CONTACT FORMS ·
LEAD GENERATION
Learners who complete all the courses will earn a certificate of completion.

description:
Are you interested in joining a book club but are short on time?  Then join our Short Book Club, where we read titles that are 250 pages or less. Meetings are held on the second Wednesday of each month.
Our December book is
Small Things Like These
by Claire Keegan
Summary: It is 1985 in a small Irish town. During the weeks leading up to Christmas, Bill Furlong, a coal merchant and family man faces into his busiest season. Early one morning, while delivering an order to the local convent, Bill makes a discovery which forces him to confront both his past and the complicit silences of a town controlled by the church. Already a bestseller in France and certain to be read worldwide for generations to come, Small Things Like These is a deeply affecting story of hope, quiet heroism, and empathy from one of our most critically lauded and iconic writers
New members are most welcome! Please inquire at the circulation desk if you would like a copy of the book.

title: Language Exchange & Social Event @ Madison Ave Pub by Toronto Babel
description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

📩 **CONTACT:** Terry (Organizer)
💸 **E-transfer:** [tmg8@wealthsimple.me](mailto:tmg8@wealthsimple.me)

Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. Our events focus on language exchange, cultural sharing, and friendship — **not for dating or matchmaking.** Harassment and inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated. description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology.
